Millennials had Victoria's Secret and Bath & Body Works. Gen Z has Sol de Janeiro.
The body, hair, and fragrance brand, founded in 2015, has become a major player in the industry. A 2025 fiscal year report from L'Occitane Group, Sol de Janeiro's parent company, said the brand accounted for 31.6% of the group's sales. The report also described Sol de Janeiro as Sephora North America's No. 1 beauty brand and the No. 1 fragrance brand on Amazon US at the time.
Two Sol de Janeiro products have led that charge. First, millennials embraced the $48 Brazilian Bum Bum Cream after it launched in 2015, turning it into a skincare staple.
Tweens and teens have now become obsessed with the $39 Cheirosa perfume mists, the first of which debuted in 2020. The sprays have become a staple of young people's shopping hauls, holiday wish lists, and what's-in-my-bag videos.
The brand confirmed to Business Insider that its three most popular scents are Cheirosa 62, 40, and 68.
I'm a big fragrance fan myself, but I had yet to try the perfume mists. So I went to Ulta Beauty, purchased a $49 sample set of six Sol de Janeiro scents, and tested them on my skin.
Considering each mist's scent, staying power, wearability, and personal preference, here's how I'd rank them from worst to best.
I wish the Cheirosa 71 mist had more depth.
If there's one thing I love more than fragrances, it's sweet treats — so Cheirosa 71 should have worked for me.
Sol de Janeiro says the scent is inspired by the iconic Confeitaria Colombo bakery in Brazil, with notes of caramelized vanilla, toasted macadamia nut, sea salt, white chocolate, and tonka bean.
When I tried it, the mist smelled more like a gingerbread cookie to me. Then, as it settled, it transformed into something more reminiscent of a graham cracker drizzled with caramel.
Some critics of this scent say it smells like buttered popcorn. I didn't notice that on my skin.
Instead, it reminded me of a holiday hand sanitizer from Bath & Body Works. I can appreciate the scent for a moment, but I don't want it to linger all day. It's too strong and sickly sweet for me.
Cheirosa 62 is Sol de Janeiro's most famous scent, but it's not my favorite.
I'll be honest. I was never that impressed by Cheirosa 62, the scent made famous by the brand's Brazilian Bum Bum Cream.
Sol de Janeiro describes the fragrance as "irresistible and sunny." It's a nod to Brazil in 1962, when "The Girl from Ipanema" was written.
With notes of pistachio, almonds, heliotrope flower, jasmine petals, vanilla, salted caramel, and sandalwood, Cheirosa 62 is exactly that. I'd describe it as summer in a bottle.
That said, it also makes the fragrance seasonal for me. It just doesn't feel right to wear in the fall, winter, or spring.
I also think the notes lend themselves better to a richer, creamier product, like the Bum Bum cream.
The Cheirosa 39 mist stands out, which I appreciate.
If any Sol de Janeiro scent smells like buttered popcorn, I think it's this one.
This scent is meant to be beachy, as if you were lounging on a hammock with the breeze in your hair, Sol de Janeiro says. It has notes of coconut cream, toasted vanilla, tropical orchid, sandalwood, and praline.
When I first spray the mist, that combination smells like buttered popcorn on my skin. That's not any reflection of Sol de Janeiro. Perfumes smell different on everyone because of their individual skin chemistry.
But I'm not complaining. I actually like the scent. It's decadent, intriguing, and different than anything else in my fragrance collection.
The coconut and vanilla notes come through more as it settles, with florals peeking through. It takes some time, but it eventually transports me to an island.
So while I might not wear Cheirosa 39 every day, I will add it to my perfume rotation.
I feel fresh, youthful, and like I'm on vacation when I wear Cheirosa 68.
The Cheirosa 68 scent was inspired by Brazil's Tropicália Movement in 1968, which influenced the country's art, music, and culture.
It includes notes of dragonfruit, lychee essence, Brazilian jasmine, ocean air, hibiscus, vanilla, and musk.
To me, it smells sweet, sunny, and refreshing. I could see myself wearing it to the beach or for a night out with friends.
Considering my current fragrance lineup, I'll probably wear this on occasion when the weather is warmer. If I were a teen in 2026, though, I'd probably wear this Sol de Janeiro scent every day.
Cheirosa 40 reminds me of my favorite scent from Victoria's Secret.
The famous Carnaval Ball in Rio inspired the Cheirosa 40 perfume mist.
On its website, Sol de Janeiro says it's meant to be sultry and delicate, with notes of black amber plum, crème de cassis, jasmine, Brazilian orchid, vanilla, and musk.
In my experience, each of those notes comes through with a single spray of the fragrance. It's one of the most mature and longest-lasting scents in the lineup I tried.
It also reminds me of my favorite Victoria's Secret scent: Bombshell Intense. Naturally, I have to recommend it to fellow millennials looking to get in on the Sol de Janeiro trend.
I can't get enough of Cheirosa 48.
Sol de Janeiro says on its website that this scent should be as liberating as the "energy of 1948, when the bikini was first spotted in Brazil."
Liberating is accurate, but I'd also say this scent is exhilarating. Its notes blend guava nectar, coconut water, orchid, lemon, wild orris, pink musk, and vanilla.
Together, they create a fragrance that's as refreshing and exciting as a poolside drink in the summer. Still, the musk notes make it more versatile than a basic summer scent.
Cheirosa 48 is the Sol de Janeiro mist I'll be wearing year-round.

Britain will benefit from much closer trading relations with the EU even if that means giving up its ability to negotiate free trade agreements, the Scotland secretary has said.
Douglas Alexander helped negotiate deals with India and the US when he was a trade minister under Keir Starmer.
But he has told the Guardian he thinks joint trading arrangements with the EU – whether under a customs union or full membership – would be a bigger economic prize, not least because the EU has now negotiated its own similar deal with India.
When Starmer was prime minister, ministers would argue against rejoining the EU because it would mean having to abandon trade agreements with other countries.
Alexander’s comments show how much Starmer’s successor, Andy Burnham, who called this week for a “serious dialogue” on the UK’s relations with the EU, including possible re-entry, has shifted the government’s position.
Speaking to the Guardian from a trade delegation to India, Alexander welcomed the progress made since the Indian agreement came into force earlier this year, since when the price of scotch whisky in India has fallen by 10-15%.
But he said the economic benefits of trading agreements with the EU would be greater.
“In trade policy, geography still matters,” he said. “The Channel is just 21 miles wide. Our largest trading partner is and will remain the European Union in the years to come. We trade almost twice the amount with the European Union that we do with the United States, the largest single-country trading partner.”
He said: “It’s no secret that I was not a supporter of leaving the European Union, and I called out early as trade minister what I described as the ‘post-imperial delusions’ of the Brexiteers. Back in 2016, they promised a world of Britain as a buccaneering free trade nation in a world where barriers were coming down. Sadly, what we’ve witnessed in the year since is a more protectionist, more regionalised world in which barriers have been going up.
“At the time we joined the Pacific trade grouping, the CPTPP [Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership] – which undoubtedly makes a lot of sense geopolitically for the UK – our own analysis made clear that the long-term boost to UK GDP from membership is less than a tenth of 1%. If you compare that with estimates of the structural damage to the UK economy from Brexit, you get a sense of just how important Europe remains to our future trade and prosperity.
“We’re already paying a real economic price for putting up new barriers to our European neighbours who, with almost half of total UK trade, remain easily our largest trading partners.”
Alexander was speaking in Mumbai, where he was joined by the business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, and the environment secretary, Angela Eagle, as well as a group of mayors from northern England. He made it clear he did not support any particular method of achieving closer relations with the EU.
The ministers spent much of their time in meetings with Indian officials as they attempt to iron out what they say have been “teething problems” with the early implementation, especially for smaller businesses.
“There are always teething problems,” Alexander said. “We’re also having a conversation at the level of regulation to see how do we overcome non-tariff barriers that can prove to be an inhibitor to the kind of progress we want to see unless they’re addressed.”
Many in the government say a bigger prize will be to reach an agreement at next month’s EU summit, where Burnham hopes to sign new trading deals for emissions, electricity and agricultural products.
One hurdle to delivering that is the UK’s desire to discuss the protectionist “Made in Europe” policy, which British manufacturers fear will shut them out of a key market. EU leaders say they are willing to discuss British entry into that scheme, though they are also pushing for the UK to impose tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles, without which they fear the UK will become a back door into the European market.
Reynolds told the Guardian this week he would not impose tariffs simply because of pressure from Brussels.

Speaking to India Today, political analyst Badri Narayan analysed the political and social impact of the Indian Air Force's 94th anniversary air show, 'Wings Over the Ganga', held in Varanasi alongside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit. Narayan noted that the event, coupled with the inauguration of a textile factory and a roadshow, represents a major moment for Uttar Pradesh politics by combining livelihood generation with public outreach. Describing the display as a "package of confidence", Narayan highlighted that it reinforces national feeling and demonstrates expanding defence infrastructure and capabilities. He further explained that such initiatives promote "developmental politics" by addressing the needs of women, marginalised groups, and job seekers. According to Narayan, linking the beauty of the Ganga with the skies not only sparks widespread curiosity among citizens but also fosters a broader sense of national resurgence ahead of the upcoming elections in the state.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the Indian Air Force air show held over the Ganga at Namo Ghat in Varanasi, celebrating 94 years of the force with 94 aircraft performing aerobatic formations. Fighter jets, transport planes, and rescue helicopters participated under the theme Wings Over Ganges. The visit also carried political significance ahead of the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, as the Bharatiya Janata Party intensifies its outreach in the Purvanchal region. Alongside the aerial display, the Prime Minister held an informal roadshow from the police lines to Namo Ghat, met local representatives, and interacted with around 300 women following the inauguration of an Arvind Mills textile facility aimed at creating employment. Political analysts noted that the event coincides with heightened activity across Purvanchal, where senior party leaders plan further visits to consolidate electoral support in areas outside Varanasi.

He noted that such displays showcase India's air power, pointing out that few countries field large aerobatic formations like the nine-aircraft Suryakiran team. Recalling past military actions including Operation Sindoor, he asserted: "World needs to learn from us how to start and stop the war when you have a clear-cut aim already set." He explained that the deployment of diverse aircraft—spanning tactical and strategic transport fleets like the C-17 to fighter jets—demonstrates vertical envelopment capabilities to citizens and global observers, including regional adversaries. Group Captain Vinod also emphasised that air shows inspire youth to pursue careers as aviators and deepen public understanding of the nation's military strength.

Following the inauguration, the Prime Minister interacted with women employees at the site. The visit also featured the Indian Air Force's aerial display, Wings over Ganges, marking the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force over Namo Ghat and the river Ganga. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and cabinet ministers attended the celebrations as fighter aircraft, including Rafale, Jaguar, and MiG, alongside helicopters such as Chinook and Mi-17, conducted flypasts and aerial manoeuvres witnessed by thousands of residents gathered across the riverbanks.

Reliance Industries’ digital services arm Jio Platforms’ IPO was subscribed 6.76X as of 11:48 IST on the third and final day of bidding, with institutional investors continuing to drive demand. Investors bid for 133.51 Cr shares against 19.75 Cr shares on offer, according to BSE subscription data. The overall subscription rose from 5.57X at the end of the second day. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) subscribed their allotted portion 14.18X, placing bids for 69.49 Cr shares against 4.90 Cr shares reserved for the category. Within the institutional segment, domestic financial institutions, including banks and insurance companies, bid for 34.51 Cr shares, followed by foreign institutional investors at 26.19 Cr shares and mutual funds at 4.36 Cr shares. The non-institutional investors’ (NIIs) portion was subscribed 9.17X, receiving bids for 33.44 Cr shares against an allocation of 3.64 Cr shares. Within this category, the portion for bids exceeding ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 10.50X, while that for bids above ₹2 Lakh and up to ₹10 Lakh was booked 6.52X. Retail investors bid for 16.96 Cr shares against 8.50 Cr shares reserved, translating into 1.99X subscription. Meanwhile, the employee and shareholder portions were subscribed 2.46X and 5.59X, respectively. Inside Jio’s Mega IPO Jio Platforms has set a price band of ₹1,065–₹1,119 per share for the IPO, which opened on October 21 and closes today. At the upper end, the ₹30,213 Cr (about $3.2 Bn) offering surpasses Hyundai Motor India’s ₹27,870 Cr issue to become India’s largest IPO and values Jio Platforms at around ₹10.3 Lakh Cr (about $108 Bn). Ahead of the public issue, Jio Platforms raised ₹8,109.8 Cr from anchor investors by allotting about 7.25 Cr shares at ₹1,119 apiece. Participants included HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund, BlackRock, the Government of Singapore, and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to 27 Cr equity shares, with no offer-for-sale component. Jio plans to use ₹27,500 Cr to prepay certain borrowings of its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm (RJIL), with the remaining proceeds earmarked for general corporate purposes. The debt repayment makes the offering partly a balance sheet exercise, while its growth prospects depend on expanding beyond telecom connectivity into broadband, cloud services, enterprise solutions, and AI. RJIL had 533.3 Mn customers as of June 30, 2026, while Jio’s network carried around 60% of India’s wireless data traffic in FY26. Jio Platforms’ operating revenue rose nearly 15% YoY to ₹1.47 Lakh Cr in FY26, while net profit increased 15.1% to ₹30,049 Cr.

Sadhana Ravi won long jump gold at home on Saturday, but the distance she has been chasing all season remained seven centimetres away.
The Tamil Nadu athlete’s 5.93m effort secured the women’s under-20 title at the National Junior Athletics Championships at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Chennai. It was also just one centimetre short of the personal best that had brought her the under-18 crown in Bhubaneswar last year.
For the 18-year-old, the victory came with another immediate concern. Back pain had troubled her through the competition, and with the triple jump to follow on Tuesday, recovery was taking priority over further preparation.
“I probably might rest the next two days without doing any warm-up because my back is hurting a lot,” Sadhana said after her victory. “I am going to give more priority to that.”
The prospect of resting between events reflects a familiar balancing act this season. Even before the back trouble in Chennai, a persistent knee problem had required her to adapt her training while trying to improve in both jumps.
Speaking to Sportstar before the championships, Sadhana traced the knee pain to last year’s Junior Nationals, where she said she slipped slightly at the take-off board. Rehabilitation accompanied her training over the following months, but the problem continued into the new season.
There were encouraging performances along the way. In March, she competed against seniors at the Indian Open Jumps competition and raised her triple jump personal best to 13.08m. Having crossed 13 metres in training, she had expected to reach that distance in competition.
Her knee worsened again, however, and later in the season the discomfort limited how much jumping she could do in practice. Sessions relied more on a short approach, leaving fewer opportunities to assess her progress through full jumps.
Her coach, physiotherapist and strength and conditioning trainer coordinated their work to manage the knee and keep her competing. Sadhana credits that support, alongside her parents’ involvement, for helping her through the season.
She won triple jump gold and long jump silver at this year’s junior Federation competition, before adding a triple jump silver at the Asian U20 Championships. She felt she had given her full effort at the Asian meet, but was not entirely satisfied with the performance. Having already gone beyond 13 metres, she had arrived hoping to improve her personal best.
In Chennai, too, her ambitions extended beyond a place on the podium. Before the meet, she had spoken of improving her personal bests in both events. Saturday brought her close in the long jump, despite the interrupted preparation, but left the six-metre target for another competition.
Her commitment to both events has its origins in her father’s sporting background. Ravi had competed in the long jump and triple jump, although his daughter initially followed her brother Raswant Ravi into tennis, taking up the sport at five.
Around the age of 10, she decided tennis was not for her. Ravi told her about his own experience in the jumps and suggested she give athletics a try. Sadhana is careful to distinguish that encouragement from pressure: her father left the decision to her, and she chose to follow his example.
At Nehru Park in Chennai, Ravi began by helping her build strength before introducing her to jumping. Long jump came first, with triple jump added later. He coached her through her early years and still accompanies her to training.
She subsequently began working with Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu coach Bedros Bedrosian, whose changes to her technique she credits with improving her performances.
Under him, preparing for two events means giving each its own attention. Sadhana usually devotes a week to long jump and another to triple jump. Long jump sessions emphasise speed before progressing to the approach and short jumps. In triple jump, controlling her speed and entering the hop comfortably are priorities, with the hop, step and jump also practised separately.
The transition between them requires a mental adjustment as well. Familiarity with both events does not mean she can switch immediately from one set of movements to the other.
“I wouldn’t get my technique immediately. I need to sit down, focus and give a full recap of what I did in the triple jump. Then I’ll go into the event,” she explained.

Studying psychology at SRM has given her another way to understand that process. She had originally wanted to become a veterinarian, but developed an interest in psychology while studying it at school and chose to pursue it at university. Applying what she learns to sport, she said, has helped her recognise what she is doing and what she needs to change, bringing greater clarity to her training.
Her longer-term ambition remains to represent India at the Olympics in both jumps. “I am training my best, and I am not going to give up till I do that,” she said on Saturday.
For now, that ambition gives way to a more immediate task. With a long jump gold secured and the triple jump scheduled for October 27, Sadhana’s next two days will be shaped by how her back responds to rest.

Burning fossil fuels may have stopped the Earth from entering another ice age, a new study suggests. The research, published Thursday in the journal Science, uses samples of ancient vegetation and rock records to analyze the growth—and sudden retreat—of an ice cap that is the last vestige of an ice sheet that once covered much of North America.
The findings shows the Barnes Ice Cap, which covers parts of Canada’s Baffin Island, started growing a few thousand years ago before rapidly reversing course beginning in the 1960s as carbon pollution ramped up.
“A question that’s in the popular consciousness is, have we caused enough global warming to stop the next ice age from happening?” says Andrew Wickert, an associate professor of environmental science at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities, who was not involved in the research. The new research shows that “even as we were just starting to ramp up emissions, we’ve already done enough damage to cause the major North American ice sheet to already start retreating. That’s significant.”
The planet regularly goes through phases where ice extends down from the high latitudes—what we colloquially call "ice ages"—due to natural shifts in the Earth's rotation and orbit, known as Milankovitch Cycles. Those are followed by interglacial periods where ice retreats toward the poles.
The last ice age ended 12,000 years ago. At its peak, what's known as the Laurentide Ice Sheet covered all of Canada and extended as far south as New York and the Midwest. It retreated to form the Barnes Ice Cap, which covers an area the size of Delaware on Baffin Island.
Unlike glaciers, which can move, the Barnes Ice Cap is frozen to the bedrock, preserving the vegetal record of what grew around it under the ice. That quirk allowed the scientists leading the new study to glean information about how much it has grown—and shrank.
To determine when it first reached its modern size, they used an exposure dating technique to calculate roughly how long rocks several meters from the glacier’s edge had been exposed to the sky. Using measurements of Beryllium-10, an element that forms on the surface of exposed rock, the authors calculated that the ice sheet first reached the size it is today around 3,600 years ago.
Next, they wanted to see how much the ice cap had regrown from that point. To do this, they turned to the humble denizens of the tundra in front of the glacier: mosses and lichen.
“After the ice cap retreated, mosses eventually colonized this newly exposed land,” says Nicolás Young, a paleoclimatologist at the Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory at Columbia University and lead author of the new paper. “These mosses are living there, and things are normal—then, eventually, the ice cap starts to re-expand. The ice covers the moss, and kills it.” The traces of the dead moss are preserved in newly reexposed land, allowing Young and his team to piece together a timeline of how the ice has moved across the landscape.
Thanks to these records, Young and his coauthors estimate that the glacier started growing again around 2,000 years ago. This may have signaled the start of another glaciation period.
But starting in the 1960s, the ice cap has done something that wouldn’t correspond with another ice age: It started getting smaller again. The team used historic aerial photos that showed that the ice has reversed course, retreating significantly back from its new margins. The Barnes Ice Cap’s edges have retreated an average of 4 meters per year since the 1980s. That coincides with a period of rapidly increasing carbon emissions, which has caused ice to go into retreat worldwide. The ice cap offers a particularly stark example, though, given the growth prior to the 1960s.
“Modern retreat of this glacier has reversed 2,000 years of net expansion—that’s a pretty decent chunk of time,” Young says.
Meredith Kelly, a professor of earth sciences at Dartmouth, says the data gathered in the study is “awesome” and that the study shows a “clear pattern of what the ice cap was doing.” However, Kelly says that she would like to see a comparison of some of the data to other sites around the world to more fully grasp how, exactly, the Earth was moving into its glaciation period before the effects of human-caused warming kicked in. While we have a broad understanding of what kicks off periods where ice can grow, the exact mechanisms are still something that require more research.
The evidence presented in this paper, Young says, could also validate a decades-old hypothesis that has long been held up by climate deniers as “evidence” climate change is a hoax. In the early 1970s, scientists gathered for a meeting at Brown University to discuss hypotheses of when the next ice age might happen. (Young says that two of his coauthors on this paper were at that meeting.) The scientists concluded that a glaciation period was so imminent that they sent a warning letter to President Richard Nixon.
“I think this study actually helps show that scientists were right about a pending glaciation,” Young says. “
Media coverage of the meeting, as well as a colder period of weather in the 1970s, have long been pitched by climate deniers as “proof” that global warming isn’t actually happening. It very much is, though, and the new research actually adds to the evidence.

Srinagar, Oct 25: Describing Operation Trident as a major blow against drug trafficking, Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday said government agencies had launched simultaneous crackdowns at 38 locations across Assam, Mizoram and Manipur on October 23, busting an international narco-cartel.
“Modi government deals another lethal blow against drugs with Operation Trident,” Shah said.
He said the operation has uncovered hawala transactions worth Rs 100 crore, led to the freezing of 1,424 bank accounts, the attachment of properties worth Rs 17.82 crore, the seizure of 500 detonators and Rs 12 lakh in cash, and the arrest of 18 people.
According to Shah, the network trafficked narcotics across the borders of India, Myanmar and Bangladesh through the Death Triangle Corridor.
He said the operation reflected India's resolve to eradicate every drug network by December 31, 2029, adding that the fight against drug cartels would continue until they were completely dismantled.
Shah congratulated the anti-narcotics team, comprising central agencies and police forces from the three states, on the successful operation.

You can build a portfolio website for free without coding using AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Google AI Studio, or Perplexity. Simply provide your details or resume, ask AI to create a personalized website, download the HTML file, and publish it for free using Netlify Drop or GitHub Pages.
A resume is a standard way to showcase your skills and experience while applying for jobs. Most companies still evaluate candidates through resume screening. However, resumes follow a standard template and don’t truly visualize users’ skills.
On the other hand, portfolio sites have become popular for showcasing candidates’ creative skills. However, most portfolio sites were previously limited to developers with web development and website-publishing skills. But thanks to AI, that restriction no longer applies to regular users.
Anyone can now create a personalized portfolio website to showcase their skills and experience creatively without writing code. Web hosting services like Netlify and GitHub also make it easy to publish a simple portfolio site for free.
If you are a beginner, have never written code, and want to publish a portfolio website to showcase your skills and stand out, this guide will show you how to create one for free.
I will show you how to create a free portfolio website using Claude, ChatGPT, Google AI Studio, or even Perplexity, then guide you through a detailed, step-by-step process to publish it for free without writing code.
Table of Contents
How to Create and Publish a Portfolio Website for Free Using AI
How to Create a Free Portfolio Website Using Claude
You can create a portfolio site using any free AI model. First, let’s create one using Claude. If you’re not aware, Claude also offers a limited free version, enough for most users to create a great portfolio site.
Step 1: Go to Claude.ai and sign in or create a free account.
Step 2: Once you’re done, paste this prompt into the prompt box and press Enter. You can modify the prompt to add or remove details, or to guide how your portfolio website looks. Remember that the possibilities are endless. Even if you generate a site, you can edit and customize it later, but the free version is very limited. So, ensure that you specify every detail before submitting your prompt.
Step 3: Now wait for Claude to create your portfolio site. You will see a message such as “Creating site.html” with a timer. Leave the tab open until it finishes creating.
Step 4: Once it’s done, Claude shows a preview of your website in the side panel canvas. You can preview what Claude built. You can also see how it looks on different devices, including mobile, and whether it’s responsive.
Step 5: Next, you need to download the file. To do that, in full screen, click the small arrow icon next to the copy icon at the top right of the screen, then choose Download as HTML and save the file locally on your device.
Once the site is created, you can publish using the steps below. You can also create portfolio websites with other free AI tools like ChatGPT, Google Gemini AI Studio, and more. Those offer better free rate limits than Claude.
How to Create a Free Portfolio Website Using ChatGPT
Unlike Claude, ChatGPT offers a completely free version with much more generous rate limits, letting you create a fully personalized portfolio website.
Step 1: If you don’t have a ChatGPT account, go to chatgpt.com and sign in with your free account.
Step 2: Now, enter the prompt in the prompt box and press Enter.
Step 3: Wait for ChatGPT to plan, build, and write the code.
Step 4: In my case, building a portfolio site took six minutes. You can tap the HTML file to preview it. Like Claude, ChatGPT also opens it in a preview.
Step 5: However, it also offers a direct download option, and when it’s done, click on the download portfolio.html, and it opens a preview, and click on the download icon at the top panel, and select HTML option, and save it locally on your device.
How to Create a Free Portfolio Website Using Google AI Studio
Next, let’s build a free portfolio site using Google AI Studio.
You can also use Gemini to create a website, but here I am using Google AI Studio. It gives access to the latest models, is free to use, and offers plenty of customization options. However, if you are a beginner, it can sound complex, so we created this simple guide to help you understand Google Gemini AI Studio.
Step 1: To create a portfolio website using Google Gemini AI Studio, go to aistudio.google.com and sign in with your Google account. Next, in the sidebar, under the Build section, tap on New app.
Step 2: Now Google AI Studio directly shows the preview on the right side. Since Google offers free rate limits, you can re-enter the prompt and make the changes you want. To proceed, click the code icon at the top of the preview.
Step 3: Now find the index.html option. Google AI Studio creates several project files, but index.html holds your entire website. In the file list, hover over index.html, click the three-dot menu next to it, then click Download.
Step 4: Once downloaded, open the file from your downloads folder and check that everything works properly without breaking anything. However, I highly recommend skipping the Export and Publish options here. Export lets you download the whole project, while Publish hosts the app within Google; both steps are unnecessary if you want to publish a simple portfolio site.
How to Create a Free Portfolio Website Using Perplexity
Next, you can also build a website using Perplexity. The free version allows you to create a simple portfolio site.
Step 1: To do that, go to Perplexity.ai, sign in with your free account, and click on the Ask Anything box.
Step 2: Paste the prompt and tap Send.
Step 3: Wait for Phubloxity to create a portfolio website. Once done, it will show you the portfolio.html file. Click on it to preview.
Step 4: After you check the preview, click the download option, download it as an HTML file, and save it locally on your device.
How to Publish Your Portfolio Website for Free
To publish your portfolio site, there are plenty of options, but in this guide, I will show you two free, reliable options: Netlify Drop and GitHub Pages.
Method 1: Publish Your Portfolio Website Using Netlify Drop
Step 1: Create a free Netlify account. First, go to netlify.com and sign up with your email. You can also sign up using Google or GitHub.
Step 2: Go to app.netlify.com/drop and drop the index.html you created using Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google AI Studio from your downloads folder, or click the file and select it.
Step 3: Next, it automatically creates a free address. After a few minutes, your project shows as published with a random address such as sunny-tulip-tf52.netlify.app in my case. You can also click on that link to see the live site.
Step 4: However, if you think it can have a better name, open the project settings and change the project name to something short, such as meera-ai. Your address becomes meera-iyer.netlify.app. Make sure your site name is unique, since there will be hundreds of free Netlify sites out there.
Step 5: Once you have hosted the site successfully, you can share your link. Your portfolio is now live for anyone on any device to access it.
Method 2: Publish Your Portfolio Website Using GitHub Pages
Now let’s look at how to publish it for free using GitHub Pages.
GitHub also lets you host a simple website for free, and you can do everything on the GitHub website without installing anything. However, it takes a few more clicks than the Netlify Drop process.
Step 1: First, create a GitHub account. To do that, sign in to your free account at github.com, then go to github.com/new and create a new repository. For example, you can create ramesh.portfolio and set it to public. Remember that free accounts need a public repository for Pages to work. Turn on “Add a README” and finally tap on Create repository options.
Step 2: Once done, you can upload a file to the repository. Click Choose your files or drag and drop the index.html file, and at the bottom type a short message such as “Add portfolio website” and click on the Commit changes button.
Step 3: Once done, open the repository and go to Settings. Then click Pages in the left sidebar. Under Build and deployment, set Source to Deploy from a branch, pick main and / (root), and click Save.
Step 4: Now wait until GitHub says the changes can take up to 10 minutes. Wait for your site to go public, refresh the page, and wait for it to update. Once it’s done, click Visit site.
That’s it. GitHub will create your page under your name using a GitHub subdomain.

Geneva 17 October 2024 – This afternoon, His Excellency Mr Jérôme Bonnafont, Permanent Representative of France to the United Nations in Geneva, and WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus met in the WHO headquarters for the signing of seven contribution agreements.
The contribution totalling €24 million comes through the Ministry of Europe & Foreign Affairs. It fits in the France–WHO Framework Agreement for 2020 to 2025, which provides both a strategic framework for engagement, aligned with WHO priorities, while providing legal, administrative and financial instruments for operationalizing collaboration.
This latest contribution includes a generous €4.5 million in fully flexible voluntary funds for the Core Voluntary Contributions Account (CVCA).
Additionally, France will support key areas of WHO’s work, addressing some of the most pressing health challenges, including non-communicable diseases (NCDs), urban health labs, One Health, funding for the WHO Contingency Fund for Emergencies (CFE), and several emergencies, such as the WHO response in Gaza, response to cholera outbreaks and mental health support in Ukraine.
France will also continue to support the WHO emergencies centre in Lyon which is playing a crucial role in preparedness and response to epidemics.
Ambassador Jérôme Bonnafont underscored the importance of this collaboration: “France remains deeply committed to supporting the World Health Organization in its efforts to tackle critical global health challenges. These agreements reflect our shared priorities of promoting health equity, responding to emergencies, and strengthening healthcare systems worldwide.”
Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of WHO, expressed his gratitude, stating, “We are immensely grateful to the French Government for its steadfast support to WHO, continued partnership and leadership in global health. This contribution will enable us to address key health threats, from non-communicable diseases to emergency response, helping to save lives and protect the most vulnerable populations.”
France is a strong supporter of a fully and flexibly financed WHO, providing leadership and support to the increase of assessed contributions to the Organization. France is also one of the co-hosts to WHO’s first Investment Round towards the mobilization of predictable and flexible resources for WHO’s core work on the Fourteenth General Programme of Work (2025–2028), approved by the World Health Assembly in 2024.
This signing ceremony marks another milestone in the strong and longstanding partnership between WHO and France, reinforcing their joint commitment to a healthier, safer world.

Welcome to Edition 9.16 of the Rocket Report! Lots of SpaceX-related news this week including a couple of Thursday shockers. In one story, the company told the US Space Force thanks, but no thanks after being offered three military launch contracts. Then, on the civil space side of things, SpaceX’s Starship may required up to 22 refuelings to support a lunar landing, a NASA safety panel said.
As always, we welcome reader submissions, and if you don’t want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar.
Miura 5 getting closer to launch. PLD Space says its Miura 5 rocket, due to undertake its inaugural launch next year, is nearing final integration, Aviation Week reports. The rocket is one of three Miura 5s the company has already manufactured, with the other two designed to qualify key system elements, CEO Raúl Torres said in an October 19 program update. PLD Space now targets a first flight of the small-lift vehicle before mid-2027.
Fully integrated stage … “Manufacturing these three vehicles has allowed our teams to work continuously across different stages of production and integration, applying the lessons learned from each qualification campaign directly to the launch vehicle,” Torres said. One Miura 5 second stage is now fully integrated to kick off system-level testing under representative operating conditions. The second stage is at PLD’s Teruel test facility for its qualification campaign, including wet dress rehearsal and a static hot-fire test.
Reaction Dynamics seeks to raise $350 million. One of three prominent Canadian launch startups, Reaction Dynamics, said it is seeking to raise $350 million to grow its staff from 68 to more than 350 people, spaceQ reports. The company is developing the small-lift Aurora rocket, which Reaction Dynamics hopes will reach orbit in 2028. Reaction Dynamics also announced plans to build a medium-lift rocket, Borealis, for a debut by 2031.
You’ve got the aurora, and the borealis … With a lift capacity of 6 tons to low-Earth orbit, Borealis would carry a little under half of the advertised payload capacity of Rocket Lab’s Neutron vehicle. “We founded Reaction Dynamics because we believe Canada should be able to reach orbit on its own terms,” the company’s founder and chief executive, Bachar Elzein, said. “Aurora is how we get to orbit in 2028. Borealis is how we deliver sovereign access to orbit, at scale, by 2031.” Both of the dates appear to be highly aspirational, but we wish them luck.
Rocket Report
Keep up with the latest in space exploration and rocket launches.
Rocket Lab sets next Electron launch date. After 97 launches of Electron, it is not exactly news that Rocket Lab is preparing for its 98th launch of the vehicle. The mission, launching three HAWK satellites for the constellation operator HawkEye 360, is due to launch as early as 07:00 UTC on Friday, October 23.
So why are you writing about it? … Two reasons. First of all, it’s worth noting that Rocket Lab continues to be only the second company to develop and frequently fly a purely commercial rocket. Secondly, we love the name of the mission, “We’re Not Hawking Around.” Kudos to the Rocket Lab team for keeping launch fun and fresh, even after moving through dozens of launches.
SpaceX says no thanks to Space Force launches. The Space Force recently tried to book rides for three future satellite missions, but SpaceX declined to offer its services, Politico reports. No other rocket companies offered to take them either, the publication reported. A top Space Force official, Brig. Gen. Eric Zarybnisky, the acting portfolio acquisition executive, acknowledged growing pains for the government and space industry as demand for rockets increases. “Temporarily, there are some things we’ll need to work through, again, as we get new providers flying,” he said. SpaceX has been declining to sign new Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launch contracts for all kinds of customers.
No one else has capacity … The three Space Force missions that didn’t find a ride were listed through the National Security Space Launch initiative. Two of the missions were for the Space Development Agency. The agency is a branch of the Space Force that’s building a network of hundreds of military satellites in low-Earth orbit to provide expanded data services, and missile warning and tracking capabilities. Other potential launch providers, United Launch Alliance and Blue Origin, are both working through setbacks with their launch vehicles. Zarybnisky remained optimistic that Blue Origin and ULA will work through their technical problems and that new competitors will get up and running in time.
Who will win the medium-lift launch race? It has been 13 years since the debut of a new medium-lift rocket in the United States, the Antares vehicle developed by Orbital Sciences Corporation. Nearly a decade and a half later, there is a new generation of medium-lift vehicles coming online, and they are starkly different from Antares, which had not just Russian engines but a core stage manufactured in Ukraine.
Which comes first … In a new article, Ars updates the status of four medium-lift rockets under development in the United States: Stoke Space’s Nova, Relativity Space’s Terran R, Rocket Lab’s Neutron, and the Eclipse vehicle being built by Firefly and Northrop Grumman. The publication also (somewhat hazardously) predicts the order in which the four rockets will make their debut.
Japanese rocket launches historic Phobos mission. Japan launched a $578 million mission Monday on a five-year expedition to land on the largest moon of Mars and retrieve samples for return to Earth, Ars reports. The robotic Martian Moons eXploration mission, known as MMX, lifted off at 3:41 pm EDT Monday (4:41 am Japan Standard Time Tuesday) from Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan.
This has been tried before … The MMX spacecraft rode into orbit atop a 207-foot-tall (63-meter) H3 rocket, Japan’s flagship launch vehicle. The rocket assigned to MMX debuted a new souped-up configuration with four strap-on solid rocket boosters, full-throttle main engines, and an extended payload shroud to accommodate the demands of Japan’s heaviest and most ambitious interplanetary mission to date. MMX is not the first mission to attempt a sample return from Phobos. Russia’s Phobos-Grunt sample return mission failed soon after launch in 2011, before it could set off for Mars. (submitted by tsunam)
Chinese rocket debris found in Midwest. In September, a Chinese rocket took off from a remote spaceport in the Gobi Desert, released 10 satellites into orbit, then reignited its engine and put itself on a trajectory to rain down debris over the American Midwest, Ars reports. The rocket’s flight on September 15 lasted between 75 and 80 minutes, and it came down without completing a full orbit of the Earth. Social media posts at the time showed streaks of fiery debris falling from the sky, heading north over Kansas toward Minnesota. The overnight spectacle was also visible on the western horizon from Wisconsin.
A surprising find … The exact time, location, and direction of the debris allowed experts to connect it to the launch of a Zhuque-2E rocket, a medium-lift vehicle built by a Chinese company called LandSpace. The rocket had launched from Dongfeng, a commercial launch zone co-located with the military-run Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwestern China, less than two hours before. The incident was largely forgotten until the last few days, when a farmer in rural Minnesota discovered a circular metal object about 11 feet in diameter lay amid the forest of corn stalks.
Arianespace targets Nov. 23 return for Ariane 6. Arianespace has announced that the next Ariane 6 launch will take place no earlier than November 23, marking the rocket’s return to flight after ground testing reportedly revealed an issue with one of its turbopumps, European Spaceflight reports. The flight will carry 36 Amazon Leo satellites aboard an Ariane 64, the rocket’s four-booster configuration. It will be the fifth Ariane 6 flight of 2026 and the tenth since the rocket’s inaugural flight in July 2024.
Situation is on track … Arianespace’s new announcement follows a report from French newspaper La Tribune, published a day earlier, claiming ArianeGroup had resolved an anomaly affecting a liquid hydrogen turbopump that had disrupted the rocket’s launch schedule. According to the report, the anomaly was first detected during an engine acceptance test shortly before the start of summer. Asked by European Spaceflight to comment on the report, an ArianeGroup spokesperson declined to address it directly and instead pointed to the newly announced launch date. “The next launch has been announced today, so the situation is on track.”
How many Starships will be required for a lunar landing? On Thursday, the NASA Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel held its quarterly meeting, during which panel member Charlie Precourt (a former NASA astronaut) spoke about risks associated with the Artemis Program and landing humans on the Moon, Ars reports. One of these is the number of refuelings required to support a Starship lunar landing.
Uncertainty remains … “With respect to Artemis IV, however, we’ve got a large number of firsts that reduce the likelihood of mission success,” Precourt said. “We need to keep our eyes on numerous required fuelings for the lander. I think the last estimate is around 22 flights.” In response to this, SpaceX founder Elon Musk replied that NASA’s safety panel estimate was not accurate. “That’s way too high,” Musk said. “Actual number will be more like 6 to 8.”
SpaceX will attempt a rocket and upper stage catch. It has been a little more than three weeks since the 14th test flight of the massive Starship rocket, which largely went well despite some issues with the Raptor rocket engine. SpaceX has gleaned enough data from that test to attempt a catch of both the Super Heavy first stage of the rocket and the Starship upper stage on the next flight, Ars reports. SpaceX founder Elon Musk said he believes success is “more likely than not” for these attempts, but he added the company is hardware rich if there are failures.
Working with the FAA … Both catches would happen at the company’s launch site in South Texas, Starbase. SpaceX is currently targeting November for this 15th test flight. One of the big hurdles is regulatory, as the Starship vehicle must return to the launch site over land, including northern Mexico. “We have had significant constructive engagement with the FAA, and we expect the license for our Flight 15 to include return to launch site and tower catch for both stages,” SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell said.
Blue Origin goes bigger on New Glenn. Blue Origin announced a major expansion of its already considerable Florida launch facilities last Friday with the intent of eventually flying more than 100 rockets a year from there, Ars reports. The company said it would add two launch pads for the New Glenn rocket, in addition to two already under construction at Cape Canaveral. The company is also investing heavily in a new manufacturing facility that will produce up to 150 upper stages for a larger variant of the New Glenn rocket.
More missions … The company also plans to procure two additional landing ships to catch and return the first stage of the New Glenn rocket (it currently has one, named Jacklyn). Finally, Blue Origin said it would add a new customer integration facility, built in conjunction with the US Space Force, that will feature four payload bays to process multiple missions at the same time. “These investments are centered on one goal: building the capacity to support more missions, more reliably, and more efficiently,” said Ian Richardson, senior vice president of operations at Blue Origin.
Next three launches
October 23: Electron | We’re Not Hawking Around | Māhia Peninsula, New Zealand | 07:00 UTC
October 23: Long March 6A | Unknown payload | Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, China | 10:15 UTC

Eric Berger is the senior space editor at Ars Technica, covering everything from astronomy to private space to NASA policy, and author of two books: Liftoff, about the rise of SpaceX; and Reentry, on the development of the Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon. California’s attorney general on Saturday rebuked the Trump administration’s efforts to quash alleged noncitizen voting, calling it “politicizing and weaponizing the law”.
Rob Bonta, the state’s attorney general, said the justice department acted at Donald Trump’s direction.
“It is once again the United States Department of Justice politicizing and weaponizing the law to attack its enemies, and it is completely improper,” he told MS Now.
Less than two weeks before the midterms, federal prosecutors called upon California election officials to verify within 48 hours a list of about 20,000 ballots belonging to suspected noncitizens. Noncitizen voting is extremely rare, but in the run-up to the midterm elections, the justice department has ramped up prosecutions of people accused of illegally voting while not holding US citizenship.
California’s election personnel have raised concern that the administration’s directive could disenfranchise citizens. Los Angeles officials said this week a “high percentage” of the individuals on the list were born in the United States.
“Trump’s DOJ is so desperate to invent ‘widespread voter fraud,’ it sent California counties lists of people who NEVER voted – and voters from the WRONG COUNTY. Absolute clown show!” California’s governor Gavin Newsom posted on social media.
“Voter intimidation has no place in our democracy,” Pete Aguilar, a congressman representing south-west San Bernardino county, said in a social media post.
The federal government’s oversight attempts come amid a national Republican effort to crack down on alleged voter fraud, particularly any cases among undocumented immigrants.
“We are asking each county election official to commit to working with us by providing the necessary information for DHS to quickly verify citizenship status. With their help, we can ensure the most secure election in California history,” the justice department said.
Bonta, the California attorney general, has raised questions about the evidence behind the suspected noncitizen ballots.
“All they provided was a list of people and nothing about why they’re purportedly ineligible. If they have such information, we would be happy to review it, but they’ve provided none,” Bonta said at a recent press conference.
The DoJ also charged 28 foreign nationals recently, accusing them of fraudulently registering to vote.
“Today’s arrests prove what we have been saying,” Bill Essayli, first assistant US attorney, said in a statement. “California is mailing ballots to noncitizens, and they are refusing to comply with federal law, which makes it a crime for noncitizens to vote. The voting rights of American citizens must be protected.”
The defendants are lawful permanent residents, who have legal status in the US but are not citizens authorized to vote.
Some state officials took no action on Friday’s letters, citing the fast-approaching election, which spurred a legal battle with the justice department. An appeals court is set to hear the matter on Tuesday.

Every morning during the Martian spring and summer, a thin and extremely long cloud emerges, only to disappear again. The wispy formation appears near the volcano Arsia Mons and gradually elongates until it reaches over 1,000 miles—about the distance from New York to Kansas City as the crow flies—before dissipating. This cycle then repeats for several months.
Since it was first recorded by a probe in 2018, scientists have been unable to find a plausible explanation for the existence of this cloud, often referred to as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC). Until now. Recently, researchers successfully modeled the cloud’s formation for the first time, their results suggesting that it may be driven by a physical process that has never been directly observed in any planet’s atmosphere.
“We found that we needed to include some exotic physics… physics that, while included in textbooks, is treated as theoretical and usually thought not to happen in nature. It certainly hasn’t been seen in action before,” Jorge Hernández-Bernal, a planetary scientist at Paris’ Sorbonne Université and lead author of the study, said in a press release. “Once we included this physics in our simulations, the AMEC emerged just as we hoped.”

Questions over an IPO and ESOPs, huge investments in quick commerce and food delivery and the pressure to deliver profits: Flipkart is juggling one too many hot potatoes for the past year. In that time, the ecommerce giant has seen 14 senior level exits, including three more VPs who are set to leave the company next. The latest executives to leave are Kanchan Mishra, VP of smartphones; Amit Sachan, VP of product and tech; and Kamal Chopra, VP of corporate, as Moneycontrol reported. While Mishra spent more than a decade at Flipkart, Sachan and Chopra have been with the company for four and five years, respectively. As their tenure shows these are not employees who had just joined the company one or two years ago in the wake of all the IPO talk. These were executives who had seen much of the restructuring at Flipkart in the post-pandemic years. Plus, these departures come at a time when the company’s employees have raised concerns over ESOP liquidity and the company’s long-awaited IPO remains without a firm timeline. It has coloured these exits with a darker tint as a result. Walmart has reportedly asked the company to prioritise profitability before going public, while the expansion of its quick commerce business, Flipkart Minutes, requires significant ongoing investments. Employees holding stock options, meanwhile, are waiting for an opportunity to cash out. Sources told Inc42 that some of these executives left as they were unable to see a clear opportunity to liquidate their ESOPs, while others moved to new jobs or wanted to start their own ventures. It must be noted that at this middle management level, Flipkart has around 30 executives in VP roles and more than a dozen senior vice presidents, so these departures will not necessarily destabilise the company, but it is a sign of bubbling discontent. ESOP Liquidity Dispute Widens In fact, sources told us that the frustration over stock options has moved beyond internal discussions, with former senior executives approaching Walmart’s board to seek a fair opportunity to realise the value of their vested ESOPs. Earlier this month, former Flipkart executives, including ex-Myntra CEO Mukesh Bansal, former chief business officer Ankit Nagori and former CFO Sanjay Baweja, wrote to Walmart’s board seeking fair treatment and a full cash-out opportunity for their vested options simply because they left the company. The issue has gained importance because an IPO has long been seen as a potential exit route for employees holding Flipkart shares or options. With the listing pushed back, those employees have little clarity on when they can realise that value. For senior executives who have spent a year at Flipkart, the delay also affects decisions about whether to stay or pursue opportunities elsewhere. While ESOP liquidity is one reason behind some departures, the company’s leadership churn is also a result of executives moving into new roles or setting up their own ventures. The founder of a unicorn startup with over 30,000 employees told us that while Flipkart has the responsibility of providing liquidity to employees, listing in a hurry to meet these demands would be a mistake. “At the end of the day, Flipkart’s management and Walmart have to do the right thing by the company. If they have already done a $50 Mn ESOP buy back last year, then they already provided some liquidity opportunity. If an employee has already made ₹10 Cr - ₹15 Cr through that, then they need to give the company some more time for the next event. But if an employee who has made a few lakhs of rupees via the buyback is upset, then the management needs to address that. What’s the point of listing in a rush, without getting a good market value?” the founder said on the condition of anonymity. Walmart Wants Profit Before IPO The fact is that Flipkart’s listing plans have been discussed for years, but the immediate priority appears to be improving its financial performance. In May 2026, Moneycontrol reported that parent Walmart wanted Flipkart to achieve EBITDA breakeven by the end of FY27 before considering an IPO or another external fundraise. The report said the decision followed Walmart CEO John Furner’s visit to Bengaluru. The reported directive adds another hurdle for a company that completed its reverse flip from Singapore to India in March 2026, ahead of a potential domestic listing. There is the looming valuation question. Flipkart currently commands a valuation of $35 Bn - $36 Bn and earlier was eyeing a valuation of $50 Bn. This valuation expectation complicates finding the right window for the listing. Walmart can afford to wait for improved financial performance which would justify the valuation, but that’s not the case with employees seeking liquidity. “In a current situation, getting a $50 Bn valuation will be extremely difficult. It is indeed a tricky position for the company,” the founder quoted above added. Others believe that Flipkart cannot go into an IPO with the narrative of a growth-at-all-costs tech startup. The company is far too mature for this. “Flipkart will likely face pushback and could be forced into a valuation haircut to land in the $25B–$30 Bn range. This will match global tech-retail multiples,” Rahul Sharma, Head of Research at Equity99 said. On the other hand, the company can position itself as a disciplined, maturing omnichannel ecosystem. “A concrete roadmap to profitability can successfully defend the $35 Bn mark that Flipkart is said to be seeking,” he added. The delay is particularly striking because other Indian ecommerce companies have already reached the public markets. Meesho listed on the NSE and BSE on December 10, 2025, following a ₹5,421 Cr IPO. Snapdeal’s parent, AceVector, listed on October 5, 2026, after a ₹420 Cr public issue. Their listing gives investors a way to set benchmarks for ecommerce, while Flipkart continues to work towards its own debut. However, the comparison also shows that going public does guarantee a strong market reception. AceVector shares listed at an issue price of ₹32 and subsequently traded below that level. For Flipkart, the question is whether stronger financial performance can support its valuation expectations without forcing the company to slow its growth plans. Flipkart Minutes Complicates Profitability Push The push to improve profitability comes amid Flipkart’s aggressive investments in quick commerce. Flipkart Minutes has expanded its dark store network to compete with Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto. The business gives Flipkart a way to serve customers looking for rapid delivery of groceries, electronics and other everyday products. However, the expansion requires spending on dark stores, inventory, fulfillment and delivery operations. New stores need time to build order volumes and improve their economics. Until a store reaches sufficient throughput, its operating costs can weigh on the business. Flipkart Minutes has scaled to 1,000 micro fulfillment centers across 130+ cities and 8,000+ pincodes in under two years. The current scale of Minutes’ spending is not publicly disclosed. However, its expansion presents a challenge for Flipkart as Walmart reportedly seeks EBITDA breakeven before an IPO. Now, Flipkart is preparing to enter another competitive market with its food delivery service branded eat-in by Minutes. Currently available for its 8,000 employees, will soon be available to the public by the end of this month. The food delivery business could add to Flipkart’s spending requirements. The company reportedly will use a dedicated delivery fleet through its logistics arm Ekart. Moreover, it will also require onboard restaurants and attract customers in a market where established players spend on discounts, promotions and customer acquisition. These costs could build before the service reaches sufficient order volumes to support its operations. The launch puts Flipkart in the position of investing in two businesses that require scale to improve their economics, even as Walmart reportedly wants the group to reach EBITDA breakeven before an IPO. While food delivery could bring more frequent customer visits to Flipkart’s app, it will also require spending to compete with established platforms. Losses Grow, Pressure Builds Flipkart’s financial performance will also remain under scrutiny as it works towards a potential IPO. The Flipkart Group reported an 18.2% YoY increase in consolidated revenue from operation to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr in FY26, compared with ₹1.23 Lakh Cr in FY25. Its consolidated net loss narrowed marginally by 2.1% to ₹8,468 Cr from ₹8,646 Cr in the previous year. The financial results cover the wider Flipkart Group, including Myntra, Cleartrip, logistics, and other business, rather than the ecommerce marketplace alone. The group said its gross margins rose 23% during FY26, while adjusted EBITDA improved by around ₹1,500 Cr. Adjusted operating margin improved by 230 basis points, from -7.7% to -5.4%, while adjusted operating business losses narrowed by 17%, or around ₹1,600 Cr. However, the improvement in operating performance translated into only a modest reduction in net loss. Higher finance cost, the recognition of deferred tax assets and certain exceptional items weighed on the bottom line. The ecommerce vertical, Flipkart Internet, reported a 19.3% YoY decline in revenue from operations to ₹16,295 Cr in FY26. Its net loss rose to ₹5,498 Cr from ₹1,694 Cr in FY25. A significant portion of that is likely due to the redomiciling to India which was completed in March 2026. As Flipkart works on its public market plans, the combination of profitability targets, valuation expectations and employee concerns over stock liquidity is likely to remain in focus. For senior executives weighing their next move, the absence of a firm IPO timeline leaves questions unanswered: when will the equity they have accumulated at Flipkart become liquid wealth? India’s mega dam plan to counter China faces resistance from Arunachal tribes
NEW DELHI: The Centre has sent two companies of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to Arunachal Pradesh following violence in Pasighat during protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, officials said on Sunday.The ministry of home affairs (MHA) directed on Saturday that the two companies, comprising around 250 personnel, be airlifted from Navi Mumbai aboard an Indian Air Force transport aircraft. The units are expected to reach Pasighat and be deployed by Sunday, officials told news agency PTI.The RAF is a specialised anti-riot unit of the CRPF whose personnel wear blue uniforms.Several CRPF units are already deployed in the violence-hit areas. Arunachal Pradesh also has a permanent deployment of around two to three CRPF battalions.Officials said CRPF personnel had effectively handled the protests since Friday and prevented the violence from escalating. Several police and central forces personnel were injured during the clashes, they added.On Friday night, a mob torched an NHPC office and a police station and vandalised the residences of three political leaders, including the state BJP president, in East Siang district, according to Arunachal Pradesh Police officials.
Arunachal chief minister Pema Khandu said the right to peaceful protest was an essential part of democracy, but stressed that demonstrations must remain within the bounds of the law and should not lead to property damage or disruption of public order.Describing the incidents in Pasighat as regrettable, Khandu appealed to all sections of society to maintain peace.According to a statement issued by the chief minister's Office (CMO), a 12-hour bandh in Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts over the proposed power project remained largely peaceful on Friday. However, violence broke out in Pasighat after the bandh ended and continued until 3.30 am on Saturday.Protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) turned violent in Pasighat, East Siang district, on Friday night, with "Gen Z" protesters allegedly setting fire to the NHPC office and a police station and vandalising and looting the residences of two MLAs and the state BJP president, police said.The violence continued in waves for nearly nine hours into Saturday morning, leaving "over 40 police personnel injured in stone-pelting", police said. In 2018, anatomists at the Toho University Graduate School of Medicine, Tokyo, Japan, performed a sleep deprivation experiment on lab mice. Mice usually sleep for 12 hours a day. In this experiment, researchers induced sleep deprivation using the ‘gentle handling method’ during sleep hours so that the mice could sleep only for six hours daily.
They discovered that liver fat content in sleep-deprived mice increased without total weight gain compared to another group who were allowed to sleep normally. The liver cells were stressed, and the activity of certain genes that escalate insulin resistance and fat content within liver cells also increased with sleep deprivation.
Experiment on rats
Three years later, a group of Chinese researchers at the Xinjiang Medical University went one step ahead. In this experiment, rats were severely sleep-deprived, turning into insomniacs. Liver enzymes, blood, and liver fat increased substantially. None of these changes were notable among rats who were allowed to sleep without distractions.
They also found the reason for increased liver fat in insomniac mice — the sympathetic nerves that supplied the liver, best known for their role in responding to stress and danger, were hyperactive. When insomnia was treated with a sleeping pill in these stressed rats, the liver fat was reduced with adequate sleep.
There are lessons here, of mice and men. Sleep is an underrated activity among humans. Sometimes, the intentional and forced lack of sleep ‘to increase productivity’ is advertised by men in power to showcase their self-proclaimed metahuman nature. During an interview in 2011, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said he had become a workaholic and hardly slept for 3.5 hours in a day, and that yoga and pranayama routine kept him energised and awake.
But medical science has a different story to tell. A study of nearly 55,500 people from Europe showed that those who slept 7-8.5 hours daily had higher life expectancy than those who slept less than seven hours. In those between ages 50 and 75 without sleep disturbances, the expectation of living longer without chronic disease development was significantly higher.
And yoga interventions improved overall sleep quality, efficiency, latency, and duration, contrary to all claims.
Healthy sleep
Sleep is a vital function of human life and accounts for up to one-third of the lifespan. Contrary to normal belief, during sleep, the brain is not ‘resting’ but is engaged in various activities necessary to improve well-being, increase life, and especially impact the liver. The minimum required duration for ‘healthy’ sleep is seven hours.
When 10,000 persons with sleep disorders were followed up for one year, incident fatty liver disease was noted in 14, while in those without sleep disorders, it was only six. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease association was significantly higher among persons with shorter sleep duration (less than six hours per night) and excessive daytime sleepiness. A high-quality study showed that inadequate sleep duration was strongly associated with an elevated risk of developing non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and adequate sleep helped prevent it. With every one-hour decrease in sleep time from the recommended seven-eight hours, the risk of fat deposition in the liver increased by 24% compared with those who slept adequately.
However, when people who lost sleep during the weekdays caught up on the debt during weekends (known as weekend catch-up sleep), the development of fatty liver disease reduced significantly. Compared with non-nappers, long daytime nappers (more than 60 minutes) had a higher risk of developing non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
Identification
Correlation may not be causation, but with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, which is associated with other conditions such as obesity, high blood pressure, increased waist-hip ratio, low functioning thyroid, and high blood cholesterol, studying and identifying independent associations make realistic sense.
In people who sleep less than six hours at night, have a persistently poor sleep quality, or nap more than one hour during the day, independent of other disease conditions, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease development was a strong association. The next time someone brags that sacrificing time and quality of sleep is an achievement associated with success, know that success comes with fatty liver disease. And it is not worth it.
(Cyriac Abby Philips is a senior consultant and physician-scientist at the Liver Institute, Rajagiri Hospital, Kochi)

Three people, who were arrested in connection with a suspected arson attack which killed four family members in the Republic of Ireland, have been released, gardaí (Irish police) have said.
