Two attacks in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have killed 4 workers responding to the Ebola outbreak and injured 5 others.
The attacks occurred overnight on a shared living camp in Biakato Mines and an Ebola response coordination office in Mangina.
“We are heartbroken that people have died in the line of duty as they worked to save others,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, World Health Organization Director-General. “The world has lost brave professionals.”
The dead include a member of a vaccination team, two drivers and a police officer. No WHO staff are among those killed, one staff member was injured.
“My heart goes out to the family and friends of the first responders killed in these attacks,” said Dr Matshidiso Moeti, WHO Regional Director for Africa. “We are doing everything possible to bring the injured and front-line workers in the impacted areas to safety. These constant attacks must stop. We will continue to work with the DRC Government, partners and MONUSCO to ensure the security of our staff and other health workers.”
In the last week, there were 7 cases of Ebola, down from a peak of over 120 per week in April 2019.
“Ebola was retreating. These attacks will give it force again, and more people will die as a consequence,” said Dr Tedros. “It will be tragic to see more unnecessary suffering in communities that have already suffered so much. We call on everyone who has a role to play to end this cycle of violence.”
The situation is still evolving. WHO will provide updates as new information comes in.

An Indian court has ordered the release of two leaders of India’s Cockroach movement, who were jailed last week amid a mounting state crackdown on youth-led protests.
The two leaders of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) movement, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, had spent a week in Delhi’s Tihar jail after being arrested by Delhi police last week.
On Wednesday, a special magistrate ordered that Das and Ranka be released, despite efforts by police to keep them in prison. They were made to sign a bond pledging no further breach of peace.
Their arrest came after a draconian police crackdown on a CJP march held in the capital two weeks ago, to protest alleged manipulation of the country’s electoral roll, led to the barricading of central Delhi and thousands of young people being detained.
Das and Ranka were taken into custody for a second time days later after they jumped police barricades and held up an Indian flag at a site in central Delhi that police had cordoned off.
The pair were charged with trespass and violating the peace and sent to jail for five days, which was then extended by two further days. Their detention had provoked outrage among leaders and supporters of the youth movement, who accused the government of “cowardice” for jailing CJP leaders for holding a peaceful protest.
After the magistrate’s ruling on Wednesday evening, Das said that “truth has triumphed”.
The release of the two leaders is likely to come as a blow to the ruling Narendra Modi government, which has implemented an unforgiving crackdown on recent protests that have erupted across India.

In Summary
- Earclip-style earbuds are getting very popular these days, with the likes of Sennheiser and Samsung also launching buds in this style.
- While they are more stable than conventional earbuds and are designed to let ambient sound in, earclip-style buds have their own pros and cons.
- If you are thinking of grabbing a pair of earclip-style buds for yourself, here are some important points to keep in mind about these buds, which make them very different from traditional, ‘normal’ earbuds.
Sony has released its first. Sennheiser has released its first one too. And so has Samsung. And many others – including Apple and Google – are believed to be readying theirs. We are talking about the clip-style or clip-on earbuds that are now becoming increasingly popular in the personal audio market. As their name indicates, these earbuds are shaped like clips and are attached to your outer ear, rather than inserted into your ear canal. They generally comprise two tiny cylinders, one of which is a speaker and the other of which is a battery, connected with a band, and they are designed to clip onto your ear.
Although they were first seen on the market a couple of years ago, most notably from Huawei and Bose, and were released by many budget-friendly brands, clip-style earbuds are now taking their place in the audio tech spotlight. But what makes these relatively new totally wireless earbuds different from other TWS earbuds, and should you be thinking of getting one for yourself?
Well, here are thirteen points we think you need to know about clip-style earbuds before you clip a pair to your own ears:
Table of Contents
They are on-ear and “open” and generally more comfortable
Clip-style earbuds are on-ear buds, and clip on to the outer ear like an ear cuff. This means that they lie on top of or near the ear canal, and do not go inside it, like many other earbuds. This makes them more comfortable to wear for most users – you do not feel something is inside your ear or just dangling near your earlobe.
They are light
In terms of weight, clip-style earbuds are about the same weight as general buds – about 5-7 grams, based on the design and materials used. For instance, the Sony LinkBuds Clip are about 6.4 grams each, while the Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 5 are 7 grams each, and the AirPods are about 5 grams.
They are incredibly stable and almost NEVER fall off
Clip-style earbuds are among the most stable wireless earbuds. This is because they actually “clip” on to the user’s ear, gently pressing it between a speaker and battery cylinder or sphere. As a result, they are actually attached to your ear on both ends. You can shake your head violently, and they still won’t fall off. In our book, they are as stable as earbuds with hooks that go around your ears.
No ear tip options – one size fits all
As clip-style earbuds do not go into the ear canal, there are almost always no earbud options to let you adjust for a better fit. It is pretty much a one-size-for-everyone rule out there. This can cause a few problems, as the next point will show.
The size of your ear could affect your experience
The fact that there are no size adjustment options available at all in most clip-style earbuds and that they are basically clipped onto your ear means that your experience of them could depend on the size of your ear. Those with relatively large ears might find the speaker end of the buds lying farther away from their ear canal, while those with small ears might find the speaker end coming right on top of their ear canal. There is unfortunately no cure for this, other than making the connecting band on these earbuds adjustable or flexible, which no brand is doing so far.
They come with bigger drivers…
Most clip-style earbuds come with slightly larger drivers than those seen on most TWS. While most TWS have drivers of the size of 5 mm to 8 mm, most clip-style earbuds have drivers that are 10 mm or larger. For instance, the Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless have 7 mm drivers, and the AirPods are believed to have 7.5 mm drivers, while the Sony LinkBuds Clip have 10 mm drivers, and the Moto Buds Loop have 12 mm drivers.
…but are not the loudest
The interesting part, however, is that even though they have larger drivers, most clip-style earbuds are not as loud as other TWS. This is because the larger drivers push sound towards the ear, often going past pockets of air that lie between the buds and the ear canal. Some of the sound inevitably gets lost in this, resulting in lower volume levels.
Love bass? These are not great options
We are going to be up front about it – clip-style earbuds, and in fact most ‘open’ earbuds are not for those who love audio with plenty of bass. The open fit of these buds is not ideal for bass, which sounds best in a packed setup, allowing for reverberations and rumble. Many brands attempt to tune their buds to accent the bass and even use larger drivers, but the result is seldom close to what we get from in-ear earbuds.
External noise comes in…too much external noise sometimes
One of the biggest attractions of clip-style earbuds is that they allow external or ambient sounds to come in too, and do not seal you away from the outside world. However, this is a bit of a mixed blessing, as too much external noise, combined with the lower volumes of these ear clips, can drown out audio. We would not recommend using them in very noisy conditions like traffic jams, or even in gyms with loud noises – those sounds will come right in.
And there is no ANC either, but ENC exists
As they are “open” in design terms, and are actually made in a manner to allow external sounds to come in, clip-style earbuds do not have any active noise cancellation. The microphones on them – for phone calls – do come with some environmental noise cancellation, so call quality on many of these buds can actually be quite good.
Controls can be…challenging
Thanks to their design, which makes them very small, clip-style earbuds almost always have touch controls – there is hardly any room for buttons on them. And as the buds themselves tend to be small, these can be difficult to use and get used to. One inevitably figures out a way to get them working, but they are never quite as comfortable as those on other TWS and earbuds, especially those with stems. These are best controlled from the connected device.
Perfect for those times when you need to listen to your surroundings too (offices, large families, outdoor runs, etc.)
The fact that they are light, stay securely attached to your ear, and allow some ambient noise to come in makes the clip-style earbuds perfect for those places where you need to be aware of sounds around you. They are great for offices in which you need to keep your ears open for queries and remarks from colleagues or even for ringing phones, and even for those who stay in large families and need to keep their ears open, even while listening to music. And of course, we think they are perfect for those who love to go on outdoor runs and rides, as they stay in place and give one access to one’s phone and audio (when allowed) and also keep one aware of traffic and people around one.
Not for audiophiles, gamers, or for intense listening sessions
No matter what the brands tell you, clip-style earbuds are not for those who are very serious about their audio. They seldom deliver the kind of detail and audio quality that one gets from other TWS at their price points. At the most, one can hope for a reasonable level of clarity and a relatively balanced audio signature. While equalizers can make a difference to different frequencies, clip-on style earbuds are not really for audio purists or for those who like to listen very intensely to their music. Their relative lack of volume and limited bass also mean they are not the best option for gaming or even watching films, even though some of them do come with spatial audio. They are, however, excellent for podcasts and live streaming audio, absolutely super for audiobooks, and more than adequate for casual listening.
And one more thing…
They have a special ring carrying mode
One of the biggest problems with most TWS is putting them back in their cases. You need to find the case, open it, take them out of your ears, put them back in the case, and snap it shut. All of which can take some time, especially when you are in a hurry (say, when you want to talk to someone, or get on or off the Metro). Well, that can be avoided with clip-style earbuds. Thanks to their shape, you can simply wrap a clip-style earbud around one of your fingers. Just like a ring. Don’t worry, it won’t fall off easily. No need to fiddle around trying to find their case immediately.

Halloween candy sales drop as cost of living crisis bites American households
Government data shows candy and gum prices jumped 44% over a five-year period through September

American households struggling with elevated living expenses and steep chocolate prices have driven a sluggish start to Halloween candy sales this year.
Figures from market research firm NielsenIQ reveal that candy purchases fell 6.7% in the month ending Oct. 17 compared to the same period last year.
An 11.7% drop in mid-September wiped out early-season sales gains recorded over the previous two years.
Chris Costagli, a vice president and food thought leader at NielsenIQ, said surging fuel costs have worsened concerns over affordability, curbing demand for treats.
As of Friday, the national average for regular gasoline stood at $4.29 a gallon, up nearly 40% from last year.
"I think what you’re seeing now is a consumer that’s spending so much additional money on fuel and housing and clothing and food," Costagli said.
"Some of the decisions they're making about Halloween candy, it’s not necessarily because, 'I notice it's more expensive than last year,' it's, ‘I can’t afford it this year because I've paid so much more for so many other things. I just don’t have the financial means to buy it this year.’"
Costagli noted that small bags were the only package size seeing sales growth through mid-October, while large and extra-large sizes experienced the sharpest declines.
U.S. candy prices have outpaced general inflation for several years.
Government data shows candy and gum prices jumped 44% over a five-year period through September, while overall grocery costs rose 22.5% over the same timeframe.
Discount grocer Aldi advertised a 135-piece variety pack of Mars Inc. chocolates—including Milky Way, Trix and Snickers—for $19.87 this week.
That is nearly the same price consumers paid for a 250-piece pack five years ago.
High cocoa prices are the primary driver. Global cocoa costs hit a record $10,710 per metric ton in January 2025 due to harsh weather in West Africa, which produces 70% of world supply, and speculative futures trading, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.
Although cocoa dropped to $3,241 per metric ton in March, prices rebounded in the spring after the Iran war disrupted fertilizer shipments to Africa.
The El Niño weather pattern is also expected to dampen output, bringing heat and dry conditions through February.
Costagli noted that demand remains weak even where prices have dropped. Non-chocolate treats like gummies and lollipops averaged $6.08 per pound in the nine weeks ending Oct. 17, down roughly 3% from last year, without driving a surge in sales.
Sally Lyons Wyatt, a global executive vice president and food industry adviser at Circana, said consumers are coping with high grocery bills by making smaller, more frequent shopping trips right before using items.
She questioned whether buyers are simply holding off until closer to Halloween.
"People are very intentional and thoughtful about what they want to consume, not just for holidays, but in general," she said. "I do believe we will still see softness overall with candy, but I don’t think Halloween is doomed."
The National Confectioners Association, representing producers such as Mars, Smarties Candy Co. and Ferrara Candy Co., said it remains optimistic.
"We are just now entering the peak period for Halloween and consumer enthusiasm remains incredibly strong," the group said Friday in a statement.

German police said Saturday they had detained a suspect after a fire at Adolf Hitler’s former mountain retreat, known as the Eagle’s Nest, in the state of Bavaria.
About 200 firefighters were deployed to tackle the blaze at the Nazi dictator’s remote and difficult-to-access Kehlsteinhaus residence, on the peak of Obersalzberg in southern Germany.
Firefighters saw flames rising high into the air as they approached the scene, only to find the building “completely ablaze”, police said.
“A suspicious person was taken into temporary custody,” they said in a later statement, adding that nobody was injured in the blaze.
Police spokesperson Lisa Maier said firefighters struggled to tackle the fire due to its location at an altitude of 1,834 metres (6,000 feet).
The building was only accessible with “heavy breathing apparatus”, she said.
Authorities were alerted to the fire on Friday evening, when a smoke detector triggered a fire alarm at about 9.50pm (1950 GMT), police said.
No potential reason for the fire was given, but the German media reported that the investigators suspected it was the result of arson.
As snow fell on the Alpine peak, the Eagle’s Nest was still engulfed in flames in the early hours of Saturday, a weather camera showed.
Officers blocked access to the road leading to the retreat, according to an AFP photographer.
The firefighters found no one inside the building.
Maier said police were still investigating but will hold a news conference later on Saturday.
German tabloid Bild reported that the authorities had arrested a motorcyclist they came across on their way to the scene.
Built between 1937 and 1938, the Eagle’s Nest forms part of the toxic legacy of Hitler’s Third Reich, which was responsible for the deaths of millions of Jews as well as Roma, LGBTQ people and Communists in the Holocaust.
It was designed to serve as a monument to Hitler’s rule, although the dictator rarely visited the complex.
It survived the second world war undamaged, and since 1952 has hosted an exhibition recounting the house’s Nazi history and a restaurant.

Common mistakes you should avoid when setting up your home network
Taking a few shortcuts while setting up your home network can lead to a lot of buffering later.
Setting up your home network is a process, and it's the little mistakes along the way that will hurt you in the end. One simple yet very common error is poor router placement. Nobody wants to set up one of TP-Link's big spider routers right in the middle of the living room, but it shouldn't be tucked into an out-of-the-way corner either. Home decor is important and all, but the router needs to be in a central location, or as close as you can get it without it becoming a tripping hazard.
Nearby electronics are disruptive, so you don't want to place your router next to the microwave. Cordless phones (yes, they still exist) and baby monitors can wreak havoc on your Wi-Fi signal too. If your connection runs through a corner of the house, you don't necessarily have to set everything up right there. Regardless of the modem or gateway your ISP installs, you can still set up another access point elsewhere using an Ethernet cable. Sure, it means hiding extra cable, but setting up a home network can require compromises.
When purchasing your own router, the equipment has to be a good match for your internet plan. If you're in a rural area and DSL or satellite internet is the best you can get, a high-speed gaming router is massive overkill. Consider your home's layout and the coverage you want in each room. A larger or multi-story home can benefit from a mesh system, but the placement of each is critical for proper whole-home coverage.
Using Wi-Fi for everything and overlooking your cables
Good Wi-Fi coverage throughout the home is convenient, but wireless connections are not ideal for everything. Online gaming, for instance, requires a stable, low-latency connection for best results.
Say you have five people in the home all with smartphones, plus TVs in bedrooms, a few tablets, an Echo device or two, game consoles and a gaming PC in a home office. Without considering anything else, that's a lot of devices vying for bandwidth on your home network. Why make the gaming PC fight everything else over the air when you can run an Ethernet cable from your router to your PC and avoid the slowdown of Wi-Fi?
An Ethernet cable delivers speed, lower latency, immunity to wireless interference and better security, essentially when you're prioritizing a gaming setup over everything else. Cat6a can support 10-gigabit connections over channels up to 100 meters, which is great if you have extremely high-speed internet service.
Of course, before running cables everywhere, consider where to set up wired devices. If you add more networking equipment, do it one piece at a time, confirm each stage works and label your cables. It's much easier to troubleshoot later on when you know where everything is and how it's running.
Common home network setting errors
Some common errors on the software side of your home network are easy to overlook because the internet will still appear to work fine. Using weak router security settings is one of the most disruptive and damaging. Enable WPA3 Personal if your router and devices support it. If older equipment won't connect, WPA2/WPA3 transitional mode allows compatible devices to use WPA3 while others use WPA2 Personal with AES. Don't bother with outdated options like WEP and TKIP.
If you haven't already, change your router's administrator credentials as well as the Wi-Fi password. Each serves a different purpose: the former prevents unauthorized people from administering your network while the latter controls who can join your Wi-Fi. Replace default administrator credentials with a strong password that isn't something weak like your phone number. Always keep the router's firmware up-to-date so you aren't susceptible to known vulnerabilities.
Another mistake is buying a mesh network setup or new router without checking to see how it will work with your existing equipment. Two DHCP servers handing out addresses on the same network create potential conflicts, so you'll need to use bridge mode or access point mode if you're adding another router. Network equipment instructions should walk you through the right configuration.
Keep it simple, document, and add new features gradually. That sounds a bit excessive, but it makes a huge difference if something goes wrong.

Japan's unpopular revision of Imperial law that reinforces male-only succession takes effect
Japan’s unpopular revisions to the Imperial House Law that reinforce the male-only succession rules took effect Saturday
TOKYO -- Japan's unpopular revisions to the Imperial House Law that reinforce the male-only succession rules took effect Saturday. The new rules are expected to bring historic changes to Japan's 1,500-year-old monarchy.
The changes include allowing the adoption of distant male relatives raised as commoners to become royals and father future heirs, and letting princesses keep their royal status after marrying commoners.
But the revised law bars Emperor Naruhito 's hugely popular daughter Princess Aiko, 24, from becoming his successor, and her future possible children from even becoming royals.
Critics say the revisions discriminate against people based on their family background or gender and put pressure on younger members of the royal family to produce male offspring.
The Imperial Household Agency has said officials are studying how to implement the measures.
The male-only succession rule means the line must move to the emperor’s younger brother Akishino, then to his 20-year-old nephew Prince Hisahito. Next in line after him is the emperor’s 90-year-old uncle.
The revised law allows adoption of unmarried male descendants, aged 15 or older, of distant imperial relatives — but only of paternal lineage — into a branch of the royal family.
The plan is to find candidates from families that renounced their royal status in 1947, which at the time was to ease the postwar financial burden on the monarchy. Four of the 11 such families remain, but they are at least 36 generations removed from Naruhito after splitting from a common male-line ancestor 600 years ago, officials said.
The government efforts to make sure that male royals are producing male emperors have triggered criticisms.
Conservative scholars say there are a number of candidates, but so far nobody has come forward and many are skeptical if anyone will volunteer. Experts also raise questions about the lack of transparency in the selection process.
Previously, princesses who marry a commoner had to renounce their royal status and leave the royal family. The last one who did so, though willingly, was Mako, one of two nieces of Naruhito, who married her college boyfriend in 2021 and has moved to the U.S. where he became a lawyer.
Five single princesses, including Aiko and her cousin, Kako, 31, can now choose whether to remain as royals if they marry.
The change is intended to keep female royals from leaving, allowing them to pursue their work and help in official duties as the imperial lineage ages and declines.
But experts say the effect will be limited because the law does not give royal status to their future husbands and children.
The measure raises many questions and concerns. They include wedding rituals, where the princesses should live after marriage, and whether husbands or children can accompany princesses on official duties. Experts say their main concern is a possibility that some civil rights of commoner husbands and their children could be restricted as with the royals.
Barring husbands and children from having royal status is clearly an attempt to prevent maternal-line succession, said Hideya Kawanishi, a Nagoya University professor and expert on monarchy. “We will find all kinds of issues that are incoherent.”
All but one mainstream newspaper have criticized the revisions, and media surveys show a large majority of the public support female monarchs or maternal-line succession.
Influential cartoonist Yoshinori Kobayashi, who has written political comics and supports female monarchs and maternal-line succession, calls the revised law unconstitutional and is set to file a lawsuit against the government.
Japanese people, largely conservatives who are fans of Aiko or oppose the male-line succession, have taken to the streets in recent weeks and their movement is growing.
Earlier in October, hundreds of people marched in downtown Tokyo to campaign for Aiko's succession rights and ask for another revision to the law. “Aiko-sama for crown prince!” they chanted.

Inside The Dalal Street Startup Ride Indian startups had gained a reputation for being “loss making” by prioritising growth at all costs and market share over immediate profitability. The trend of putting scale ahead of the bottom line was at its peak amid the funding boom of 2020-22. While prioritising growth is not wrong for startups, especially at early stages, the start of funding winter in 2022 gave a reality check to the Indian startup ecosystem. Subsequently, startups started pushing for profitability. Giving further wings to the aggressive profitability push was the ambition to list on the exchanges. While new-age tech companies look to turn profitable before filing their draft IPO papers, those that cross the line manage to stay in the green, data shows. Over 60 of the new-age tech companies are currently profitable. In terms of profits, Groww now leads the pack of new-age tech companies, posting a net profit of ₹2,083 Cr in FY26. Prominent internet companies Paytm and Eternal trail Groww in terms of profitability, raking in profits of ₹553 Cr and ₹366 Cr in FY26, respectively. It is pertinent to mention that these companies have been listed on the bourses for years now, with Info Edge making its public market debut in 2006. While these companies trace their origin back to the 90s, a large majority of the new-age tech stocks under Inc42's purview are about a decade old. From a broad perspective, Inc42 data reflects that the median time taken for a startup to get listed on the bourses is 11 years. While listing for 18-year-old ixigo and 19-year-old Fino Payments Bank came relatively much later, ArisInfra's IPO materialised within four years of its operations. Meanwhile, the new-age tech companies that have made their public market debuts this year generally turned profitable right before their public market debuts. For instance, eyewear major Lenskart reported a net profit of around ₹297 Cr , a significant turnaround from a ₹10 Cr loss in FY24. The company maintained profitability in FY26, raking in a PAT of ₹494 Cr in the fiscal. Urban Company also reported its first consolidated net profit of approximately ₹240 Cr for FY25, it returned to the red in FY26. For the full year FY26, the company reported a net loss of ₹234.8 Cr against a net profit of ₹239.8 Cr in previous year despite seeing a revenue growth of 36% YoY to ₹1,555.5 Cr Sectors Driving India’s Startup IPO Boom The startup sectors producing the most number of listed companies is proportional to the private funding trends witnessed in the Indian startup ecosystem. The three most funded sectors, fintech, ecommerce and enterprise tech, also house the highest number listed startups. While fintech and ecommerce house 14 names each, 13 enterprise tech startups have listed on the bourses so far. The dominance of the fintech and ecommerce sectors on the bourses is expected to continue as the likes of Tonbo Imaging, Zepto and OYO would soon be making their public market debuts. Delhi NCR Home To Highest Number Of Listed Startups While Bengaluru continues to be the startup capital of India, Delhi and its neighbouring cities Gurugram and Noida account for the most number of listed new-age tech companies. Overall, the Delhi NCR region is home to 27 listed new-age tech companies, ahead of Bengaluru's ninetineen and Mumbai's fifteen. While fifteen companies, including Eternal, Delhivery, and Lenskart, call Gurugram their home, Awfis, EaseMyTrip, MapmyIndia and E2E Networks are from Delhi. Noida on the other hand is home to six listed new-age tech companies, including Paytm and IndiQube. Delhi NCR contributes $90 Bn in the cumulative $167 Bn market cap of new-age tech companies. Women plan street demonstrations in more than 20 Polish cities and towns on Thursday (October 22, 2026) to protest the lack of access to free and legal abortion.
They're accusing Prime Minister Donald Tusk's liberal government of failing to fulfil its promise to relax Poland's strict abortion laws, and are protesting even though the Parliament passed two bills on Tuesday (October 20) aimed at easing abortion rules. The measures are likely to be vetoed by the conservative president, Karol Nawrocki.
Passing the draft laws now, a year before the next parliamentary election, is a case of “token gestures” rather than a genuine effort to reform abortion law, said Zofia Marcinek of the Abortion Dream Team, a reproductive rights activist group in Warsaw.
She said the liberal government knew the draft laws stood no chance of withstanding Nawrocki's veto, and has merely tried to create the impression of taking action because it needs women's support to win elections next year.
Most abortions are performed secretly
Since 1993, legal abortions have been allowed in Catholic Poland only in cases of severe fetal abnormality, risk to the mother's life and health, or the pregnancy being a result of rape or incest.
Also Read | Doctors decide: On legal abortion
Polish women have been pushing for the legalisation of abortion ever since, including in a nationwide wave of demonstrations of women wearing black called “Black Protest,” which began in 2016.
Rather than being liberalised, Poland's abortion laws were tightened further, banning abortions of fetuses with congenital defects in 2020 under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government.
Despite the laws, abortions remain common in Poland, an overwhelming majority of which are carried out by women at home using pills obtained from outside the country. Women who undergo abortions, including by taking pills, do not face criminal responsibility under Polish law. But people helping them, including doctors and family, can potentially be prosecuted.
And abortion remains a taboo subject in Poland, which now has one of Europe's most restrictive abortion laws, with only Malta imposing stricter limits.
Activists accuse Polish government of disinformation
PM Tusk's pro-European coalition won the 2023 election in part on a promise to liberalise Poland's abortion laws. But in 2024, Mr. Tusk said his government wouldn't be able to overcome the likely veto of a conservative president. Instead, measures were introduced to prevent hospitals from refusing to perform legal abortions on religious grounds.
"The state will increasingly effectively stand on the side of the woman when she is making dramatic decisions in her life,” Mr. Tusk said in 2024 when he announced the measures.
Polish hospitals performed 573 abortions in the first half of 2026, compared to 452 in all of 2022, before Mr. Tusk came to power, according to data from the National Health Fund. But activists say tens of thousands of abortions happen yearly outside of hospitals.
Activists organising Thursday's (October 20) protests are claiming the Mr. Tusk government has betrayed Polish women — and that PM Tusk's claims that women's access to abortion has improved during his administration have actually complicated getting care for some women.
“The government's promises act as a type of disinformation,” Ms. Marcinek told the AP. “Women getting pregnant hear the prime minister say that everything is ok, that there is access to abortion, and then they end up in the hospital and see that is not the case. So they come to us when it's very late and very complicated and expensive to help them.”
Meanwhile, international donors are less interested in supporting Polish women's rights because they mistakenly believe things have improved, Ms. Marcinek said.
Activists dispense abortion pills outside Parliament
In 2025, the Abortion Dream Team opened an “ abortion clinic ” across from the parliament building in Warsaw where women can get information about their options, or even take their abortion pills in the company of supporting activists.
This September, the activists also launched a parcel locker dispensing abortion pills at the same location, nicknamed “Abortomat."
The dispenser is operated by the international feminist non-profit Women Help Women. It enables women needing abortions to get the pills the next day, rather than wait for up to two weeks for home delivery, Ms. Marcinek said.
“There are also people who cannot safely order such pills at their own address, for example because of an unsupportive family or abusive partner," she said. “These women can get a pin number and pick up the pills in the machine the next day.”
“In Poland, assisting with an abortion is a criminal offence. Even passing the pills from hand to hand can be considered a crime,” the Abortion Dream Team wrote in a statement. "That's why we're hacking the Criminal Code and bringing abortion into the 21st century.”

Windows 11 Home is ideal for everyday tasks like browsing, gaming, and office work. Windows 11 Pro adds BitLocker encryption, Remote Desktop hosting, Hyper-V, and advanced management tools. Pro suits professionals and businesses, while Home is enough for most users. You can upgrade from Home to Pro without reinstalling Windows.
Unlike macOS, Windows comes in different versions. Windows 11 Home is the most common version designed for everyday use, while Windows 11 Pro is for professionals and business users who want maximum security and useful remote features.
Most PCs and laptops mostly come with Windows 11 Home out of the box. It is enough for most users. However, if you need specific features for enhanced device security and remote access, Windows 11 Pro is a strong option, especially for professionals who handle sensitive information and for businesses that need to access devices remotely when staff are away from home.
If you are a beginner, choosing between Windows 11 Home and Pro can be confusing, especially since they look almost identical and it’s hard to tell them apart at first. In this guide, you will learn the differences between Home and Pro and which one you should choose.
What do Windows 11 Home and Pro have in common?
Windows 11 Pro is basically an extension of Windows 11 Home. Compared to Windows 11 Home, it adds a few extra features designed for business and professionals. However, both versions share most basic, everyday features.
Starting with the interface, both look and feel similar and support the same core Windows features, everyday apps, and software. Both also support Windows Hello, Secure Boot, Find My Device, and receive frequent Windows security updates.
For security, both Windows 11 Home and Windows 11 Pro include a firewall and network protection, support Windows Hello sign-in options, and support Secure Boot on compatible hardware.
Microsoft also offers basic device encryption in Windows 11 Home on supported PCs. However, full BitLocker management is only available on Windows 11 Pro, which you can learn about in the next section.
Since every major core feature of Windows is the same, and every app runs without any issues, and both versions have support for everyday apps and software, you won’t find much difference between them if your main activities include: accessing Windows core features, browsing, video calls, editing videos, documents, streaming, browsing, and gaming. However, keep in mind that while Windows 11 Home and Pro offer the basics for everyday users, performance depends on your PC hardware, including the processor, memory, and graphics card.
Even if you initially choose Windows 11 Home, you can upgrade to Windows 11 Pro without extra hardware.
The Pro features that can change your decision
Windows 11 Pro is designed for people who care about security and want to control their PC when they are away from home. The biggest difference is BitLocker encryption: Windows 11 Home offers only basic device encryption on supported PCs, while Windows 11 Pro offers full BitLocker management, so if you lose your PC and someone accesses your encrypted storage without authorization, they can’t easily retrieve your data.
This is especially useful for businesses with confidential information, so Windows 11 Pro makes more sense. Windows 11 Pro offers BitLocker encryption and supports Remote Desktop hosting, which isn’t available in Windows 11 Home. A Windows 11 Pro-supported PC can act as a Remote Desktop host, so you can connect to it from another device when you are away from home. This is especially useful when you are away from home and want to access an important file or use an important application that’s installed on your device.
Another Windows 11 Pro-exclusive feature is Windows Sandbox, which lets you run a temporary, isolated Windows environment on your computer, especially useful for running risky applications that may contain malware and could damage or access sensitive files on your device.
Windows 11 Pro also supports Hyper-V virtual machines, where you can install another version of Windows on your laptop and test your software.
This is especially useful for developers testing your app on various Windows versions. Another major difference is the Group Policy Editor, which lets Windows 11 Pro users access admin controls and advanced Windows settings.
It is not just software; Windows 11 Pro also extends your hardware capabilities. For instance, Windows 11 Home supports up to 128 GB of memory, while Pro supports up to 2 TB. Another big difference is price; Pro costs more because of these extra features.
Checking your edition before you set up or upgrade
The best part of Windows 11 Pro is that you can upgrade from Windows 11 Home. Even if you are currently using Windows 11 Home or chose Windows 11 when buying a new laptop or computer, you can easily upgrade to Windows 11 Pro later.
To check which version of Windows you are using, go to Settings > System > About and look under Windows specifications. Then open System > Activation to check its activation status. If you are on Windows 11, you can compare the features. Nerdused carries Windows 11 product keys, and this Windows 11 Home vs Pro guide can help you review the differences as you decide.
Upgrading from Home to Pro without a clean reinstall
As I said before, you can also upgrade from Windows 11 Home to Pro without losing your files or reinstalling Windows. First, make sure Windows 11 Home is activated.
For safety, I highly recommend backing up your important files and installing all available Windows updates.
Once done, open Settings, go to System, then Activation. From there, click Change next to Change product key. Enter a valid Windows 11 product key, then follow the on-screen instructions to upgrade.
If you don’t have the key, select Upgrade your Windows, open the Store, purchase one from the Microsoft Store, then restart and follow the on-screen instructions, restarting the PC if prompted. Then return to Settings > System > Activation and confirm your device is running Windows 11 Pro.
To summarise, choose Windows 11 Home if you mainly use your device for browsing, gaming, video editing, office work, and other everyday tasks.
However, choose Windows 11 Pro if you are a professional or want advanced security features such as BitLocker encryption and remote control of your device while you are away from home. You can test different Windows versions and install one inside your current Windows. Support for features such as Remote Desktop hosting, Hyper-V, and business management tools.

As anticipation builds around Nitesh Tiwari’s upcoming film Ramayana, the makers have been taking steps to bring elements of the epic closer to audiences. As part of the film’s promotional campaign, Lord Ram’s bow has been put on display at PVR Palladium in Lower Parel, Mumbai, offering visitors a glimpse of an artefact inspired by the world of the Ramayana.
Ramayana Promotion: Lord Ram’s grand bow on display at PVR Palladium in Mumbai
The bow, showcased inside a specially designed glass enclosure, has been presented on an ornate black display table featuring intricate golden carvings. Set against a red velvet base, the weapon features detailed gold-toned craftsmanship, decorative motifs and curved ends. The display also carries the Ramayana title, along with the names of producer Namit Malhotra and director Nitesh Tiwari, connecting the installation to the upcoming cinematic adaptation.
The installation stands out within the cinema premises, where the elaborate presentation draws attention to the film’s mythological setting. The display combines traditional Indian-inspired design elements with a contemporary promotional setup, creating a visual attraction for moviegoers visiting the venue. Its placement at PVR Palladium also brings the film’s promotional activities into a public space where audiences can encounter an element associated with the epic beyond the screen.
The bow display forms part of the broader promotional efforts surrounding Ramayana, which is being directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. The film is among the major cinematic adaptations of the Indian epic being developed for the big screen. By showcasing the bow at a cinema venue in Mumbai, the promotional campaign draws on an important symbol associated with Lord Ram and the story’s cultural significance.
The installation also offers a visual introduction to the film’s world, with the display’s elaborate detailing reflecting the traditional aesthetic associated with the epic. For visitors at PVR Palladium, the bow serves as a physical promotional centrepiece connected to the upcoming film.

Israeli settler group submits proposals for new Jewish settlement in Sheikh Jarrah neighbourhood
An Israeli settler movement has submitted an application for a new Jewish neighbourhood in the Sheikh Jarrah area of East Jerusalem.
The Amara movement submitted a proposal to the planning association to build a Jewish neighbourhood comprising 122 housing units at the former site of the Shepherd Hotel.
The Shepherd Hotel, often referred to as the "Mufti's House", was originally built in the 1930s for the former mufti of Jerusalem, Haj Amin al-Husseini, though he never actually lived there. It was demolished in 2009.
The application is scheduled for an initial hearing before Jerusalem’s Local Planning and Building Committee on 11 November.
Founded in the 1970s, Amara has been one of the prime driving forces behind settlement expansion in the occupied Palestinian territories, but this latest development would be its first settlement in Sheikh Jarrah.

A Bengaluru-based private hospital has launched a campaign encouraging women to make breast awareness part of their monthly routine, with a simple reminder to look for changes, become familiar with how their breasts normally feel, and seek medical advice if anything unusual is noticed.
The nationwide campaign, ‘Left Right Kiya Kya?’, was launched by HCG Cancer Hospitals with the aim of extending breast cancer awareness beyond October, when campaigns typically focus on the disease. It encourages women to spend three minutes every month paying attention to both breasts.
According to the International Agency for Research on Cancer’s GLOBOCAN 2024 estimates cited by the hospital, India recorded about 2.37 lakh new breast cancer cases and 96,100 deaths in 2024. Breast cancer accounts for about 30% of new cancer diagnoses among women in the country.
The campaign uses the familiar words ‘left’ and ‘right’ as a reminder to check both breasts and recognise unusual changes. It includes music and an AI-generated film featuring women in everyday situations. An on-ground activation at Nexus Seawoods in Navi Mumbai featured a live musical performance by women dressed in pink, followed by a doctor’s demonstration on recognising breast changes.
Recognising changes
The campaign encourages women to look for changes in breast size, shape or skin, check for unusual changes around the breasts or nipples, and become familiar with how their breasts and underarm areas normally feel.
Jayanti Thumsi, Group Lead, Robotic Breast Surgery, at the hospitals, said some women sought medical help only when their cancer was advanced, while others noticed changes but did not act on them.
“Most breast changes are not cancer, but they should never be ignored. If you notice a lump, unusual nipple discharge, or any other change, consult a doctor without delay, rather than waiting for your next monthly reminder,” she said.
She added that breast awareness did not replace screening, and mammograms should be planned according to age and individual risk.
Manu Sankar Das, Chief Marketing Officer, HCG Cancer Hospitals, said the campaign was designed to make breast awareness a recurring habit rather than an annual reminder.
“Awareness that lasts only through October isn’t enough. It needs to become a reminder that comes back every month. Left breast. Right breast. Three minutes, once a month,” he said.

The Ohio senator who has been the subject of President Donald Trump’s constant praise for his physique has revealed how he feels about the comments.

17 Kuki militants under SoO deal arrested in Manipur; mismatch found in identities
The operation was carried out in Mt Sinai Camp, Saimol village, a day after three persons from the Meitei community were killed in an attack.
Seventeen cadres belonging to Kuki militant groups under the Suspension of Operation (SoO) agreement were arrested on Saturday during three days of security forces' operation at a designated camp in Manipur's Kangpokpi district. Police informed that their identities didn't match the registered cadres of groups under the SoO deal.
The operation was carried out in Mt Sinai Camp, Saimol village under Saikul police station, a day after three persons from the Meitei community were killed and three others injured during an attack in Khongban Sunulok village of Imphal East on October 19.
Security forces recover 24 automatic weapons, ammunition
According to the officials, Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA) commandos, an elite special operations unit of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), assisted by other security forces and Manipur police, carried out an unprecedented special inspection and search operation in Mt. Sinai camp (a Kuki militant-designated camp established for SoO cadres).

A senior security officer requesting anonymity told HT, “The operation was launched on Tuesday and continued for around 90 hours till Friday. In the said operation, including its surrounding areas, security forces have recovered 24 automatic weapons of various calibres, including one SLR, one A1rifle, three G3 rifles, 2 lathodes, thirteen AK series rifles, one M15 rifle and two M16 rifles. Additionally, 1061 rounds of 7.26 X 39 mm calibre, 2,350 rounds of 5.56 mm INSAS rifles, 223 rounds of 7.72X51 mm, thirty-four magazines of different weapons, 19 wireless sets and other war-like stores.”
During inspection and physical verification of the cadres, the identities of the 17 cadres comprising 8 persons belonging to ( Kuki National Organisation/ Kuki National Army (KNO/KNA) and 9 persons belonging to Kuki National Organisation/ Kuki Liberation Army (KNO/KLA) were found doubtful and could not be authenticated against the record of registered SoO cadres, said the same senior security officer.

Officials said the camp is under the occupation of central forces.
A second security officer aware of the matter said the whereabouts of the cadres listed as being stationed at the camp remain untraceable.
17 accused remanded to eight days of police custody
According to police, FIRs are being registered under relevant provisions of the BNS, Arms Act, Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act and Explosive Substances Act against all 17 arrested.
Manipur police on its official X account stated that “all the 17 accused have been remanded to 8 days police custody till 31/10/2026. Their medical examinations have been completed.”

Manipur Home Minister Govindas Konthoujam had expressed to the media on Friday here in Imphal that the SoO pact with Kuki militants is not extended since its expiry on September 4, 2026. Quick Answer
A VPN is better for privacy and security because it encrypts your internet traffic and hides your IP address. A proxy only masks your IP address without adding encryption. Use a VPN for secure browsing, especially on public Wi-Fi, and a proxy when you simply need to hide your IP address or access restricted content.
VPNs and proxy servers are still commonly used to hide your IP address and access restricted content. However, there is still a lot of confusion about what a proxy can do versus what a VPN does; a VPN works differently. If both change your IP address for more privacy, why choose one over the other?
That is exactly what you will learn in this guide. You will learn what a VPN does, what a proxy server does, the biggest difference between them, and which one you should use.
At a high level, Both VPN and proxies mask your real IP address. Both act as intermediaries between your device and the internet. Instead of connecting directly to the internet, your traffic first goes through another server.
The biggest difference is how this server handles your data. A VPN server encrypts your traffic, while a proxy routes it through a dedicated server without encrypting it.
Table of Contents
How VPN and Proxy Servers Work
What is a proxy?
A proxy is even simpler. A proxy server is a dedicated server that your device connects to first before it connects to the internet.
Let’s say you want to visit techpp.com. Without a proxy, your device directly connects to techpp.com, but with a proxy server, your device first establishes a connection with a proxy server, and the proxy server then connects to the website on your behalf.
Since your device is not directly connected to the website and fetching data, the website like ours, techpp.com, only sees the proxy server’s IP address instead of your original IP address.
And this is where the biggest difference between a VPN and a normal proxy lies.
Unlike a VPN, a proxy server won’t encrypt your data. It won’t create a secure private tunnel between your device and the proxy server. So if any hacker intercepts your connection between your device and the proxy server, they can see exactly what type of data is being transferred, and your internet service provider can also see what kind of data is being transferred between your device and your proxy server and which proxy server you are connected to.
There are different kinds of proxies. A normal HTTP Proxy mostly handles web traffic, whereas a socks5 proxy can handle different kinds of traffic, including browsers, games, email, and more. more. It also supports TCP and can forward UDP traffic. Another thing you should be aware of is proxy bandwidth; some providers charge based on how much data you transfer, while others offer socks5 proxies unlimited bandwidth.
Simply put, a proxy server changes the route your traffic takes, while a VPN does the same but also encrypts the connection between your device and the VPN server.
How does a VPN work?
A VPN (Virtual Private Network) encrypts your outgoing and incoming data from your device.
Normally, when you connect to the internet, your data passes through your ISP (Internet Service Provider) before reaching out to the website or the service you want to use.
Since the data is not encrypted, your ISP can see the websites and services you are connecting to.
But modern web requests today are routed through using HTTPS, which is already a secure way of connecting where your data is already encrypted. Since the data is encrypted, your ISP cannot see passwords, messages, or the exact contents of an HTTPS page. But your ISP can still see information about your internet connection because the requests are coming directly from your device’s IP address.
However, when you use a VPN, your device first connects to a VPN private server and establishes a secure tunnel. Once the connection is established, your data first travels through this encrypted tunnel. The VPN server then connects to the website or the service you requested on your behalf.
Your internet service provider won’t be able to see which service and data you are requesting from your device and only sees VPN Server requests and an encrypted connection between your device and the VPN server. Also, the service and the website you request see the VPN’s public IP address instead of your real IP address.
However, using a VPN does not entirely secure your connection, as some VPN service providers have a policy of logging your data. However, it also largely depends on the data logging policies, VPN protocols, security practices, and the reputation of the VPN provider you are using.
We have a detailed explanation of how VPN works and also an interactive guide to help you learn more.
VPN vs Proxy: Which One Is Faster?
Speed entirely depends on the individual server capabilities, but in general, a VPN follows one extra step of encrypting and decrypting your data, so in general it makes it slower. However, modern VPN devices and protocols can handle this process very quickly.
On the other hand, since a proxy directly routes your data without encrypting, it is generally faster.
But the speed entirely depends on the individual server capabilities, including the server location, server load, internet connection, and the VPN or proxy service you use. For instance, a proxy server handling more requests than it is capable of can be slower than a VPN. And a VPN server located on the other side of the world can be slower because your data needs to travel a longer distance, which adds latency
VPN vs Proxy: Which one to use?
If privacy is important, a VPN is generally a better option to go for.
Choosing a VPN or proxy entirely depends upon your type of use case. Since a VPN secures your connection by encrypting your data, it is best used on public Wi-Fi and if you want to hide your data from your internet service provider.
A proxy is most useful if you are accessing geo-restricted content and you want to hide your IP address, since you are using the proxy server’s IP address to browse the internet. Your real IP address is hidden.
Also, remember that a VPN is capable of everything that a proxy server does because it also masks your IP address and can also unblock geo-restricted websites since you are using the VPN’s IP address to access the internet.
VPN vs Proxy: Quick Comparison
Final Words
This is a quick, detailed comparison of the biggest differences between a VPN and a proxy based on real-life scenarios. These are the biggest differences, including speed differences and when to choose a VPN or a proxy server based on your use case. To sum it up, use a VPN for better privacy, and use a proxy if you simply want to hide your IP address.

Much of what we know about how a brain makes decisions comes from studying monkeys watching dots. In a task known as a random-dot-motion task, a cloud of flickering specks drifts weakly in one direction while the subject tries to determine whether—and in which direction— it’s moving. The task has shown that in the primate neocortex, neurons gather visual evidence over time, with their firing rates climbing until they cross a threshold, when the animal commits to a decision.
But avian brains don’t have a neocortex, so it wasn’t obvious how they made similar decisions.
“This was the big question,” said Andreas Nieder, a neurobiologist at the University of Tübingen. “How [would] a differently organized avian brain encode decisions?”
To find out, Nieder and his colleague Philipp Schmidbauer put two carrion crows through the same task the monkeys faced, recording their brain activity along the way. The crows solved the task the same way primates do, using the same mathematical logic despite having a very different brain structure. And they did it two times faster.
A brain built different
Nieder and Schmidbauer put two hand-raised crows in front of a touch-sensitive monitor showing a cloud of white dots on black, with some fraction of them drifting coherently left or right or up or down. The birds’ job was to report the overall direction by pecking one of targets that flanked the display. Correct answers earned them a mealworm.
“We intentionally wanted to have exactly the same random-dot motion task,” Nieder said. “The only difference was that the crows had to peck to indicate their decision, whereas monkeys were indicating by making an eye movement.”
The researchers varied how many dots moved together, ranging from 81 percent of the dots coherently moving together, which is trivially easy to determine, down to 3 percent, which is barely distinguishable from noise. They also included a zero percent condition, in which there was no correct answer.

Which iPhone Should You Buy (or Avoid) Right Now?

Apple sells seven iPhone models, from the $699 iPhone 17e to the $1,999 iPhone Duo, but which iPhone is best for you? This is a good time of the year to buy an iPhone if you need to upgrade, since Apple just released its flagship models. (We don't expect the more affordable iPhone 18 models until spring 2027.) But First, Sell That Old iPhone!
If you’re upgrading from an iPhone, you can trade it in to Apple for a small discount. Before you do that, check whether you can sell it elsewhere for more money. iPhones hold their value incredibly well, particularly if they’re in mint or good condition. We have a guide that runs through the process of selling your phone, and we generally recommend you use websites like Swappa, Gazelle, or Back Market.
We also have a handful of setup guides you should follow:
Buying From Apple vs. a Carrier
Most people in the US purchase iPhones from carriers, which means the devices are locked to that network. If you bought an iPhone from Verizon, you can't easily switch to another carrier without breaking a contract and paying extra fees. It also poses headaches for travelers who want to use international SIM cards or eSIMs.
The easier approach is to buy directly from Apple, though there are some things you should know:
Connect to any carrier later: Choose this option for the most hassle-free experience. You get an unlocked iPhone, then all you need to do is transfer the SIM card or eSIM from your old iPhone to the new one to get started. This might be painless, though you may need to contact your carrier if the iPhone can't complete the eSIM transfer. In the US, Apple hasn't included a SIM tray since 2022's iPhone 14.
Choose a carrier: If you choose a carrier through Apple.com, you will get an unlocked iPhone, no matter which carrier you choose (except if you purchase with AT&T on an installment plan). The downside is that Apple doesn't have the same offers as the carriers, so you may lose out on a deal. However, carrier offers often require new lines, trade-ins, or an upgraded plan, and the savings come in the form of bill credits, so these deals aren't as amazing as they may seem.
Finance: You can finance your iPhone either with Apple's credit card via monthly installments or as Apple iPhone Payments via a Citizens One loan. You need to choose a carrier here, but Apple confirmed these devices are all unlocked. You have to fill out a credit application to see if you qualify. If you opt to finance through a carrier on Apple.com, only the T-Mobile and Verizon models will be unlocked. The AT&T and Boost Mobile options are locked iPhones, so it's no different from buying it on an installment plan directly from those carriers.
Apple Upgrade: Buying directly from Apple also nets you access to the Apple Upgrade leasing option. Is it worth it? Broadly speaking, no. Most people do not need to upgrade to a new iPhone every year or two. It's expensive, and you must return your leased iPhone in good condition to avoid additional charges. AppleCare is not included, as it was with the discontinued iPhone Upgrade Program.
What Is Apple Intelligence?
The most hyped-up feature from the iPhone 16 range was Apple Intelligence, which rolled out in iOS 18.1. This is Apple's suite of AI features, following the wave started by the likes of ChatGPT and Google's Gemini. Apple Intelligence is available on the iPhone 15 Pro/Pro Max and newer, including the iPhone 16e (not to mention select iPads and MacBooks).
What exactly is Apple Intelligence in the first place? It's a collection of features that draw on the power of large language models to introduce “smart” capabilities. For example, in the Voice Memo and Notes app, you can now start a recording and get a real-time transcription. You can even record a call and get the transcription saved in the Notes app. Siri has been redesigned to understand when you misspeak and can even plug into ChatGPT for more powerful responses to open-ended questions. There are writing tools available throughout the operating system that let you change the tone of your emails or proofread text so you don't make an unnecessary typo on Threads.
This is just a small sampling. We've boiled down many of the Apple Intelligence features here, and additional features keep rolling out in iOS updates. For example, Genmoji—which lets you create your own emojis—debuted alongside the AI image-generation app, Image Playground, in iOS 18.2. In iOS 27, Apple added the revamped, conversational Siri AI assistant. Siri now understands personal context and can retrieve information from your messages, emails, and photos. It can also act on your behalf to draft a message with a particular tone or find a good restaurant for your partner's birthday dinner. Here's everything you can do with Siri AI.
If you don't care for Apple Intelligence and want to turn it off, you can! We have a helpful guide detailing the exact steps.
What Is MagSafe?
Magnetic MagSafe wireless charging is available on the iPhone 12, iPhone 13, iPhone 14, iPhone 15, iPhone 16, iPhone 17, and iPhone 18 models (except the iPhone 16e), and it allows you to magnetically attach various accessories to the back of the iPhone. (iPhones support Qi2, which is the open standard, whereas MagSafe is proprietary; you can use Qi2 accessories just like MagSafe.)
You can get first-party accessories like Apple's MagSafe Wireless Charger, which sticks to the back for faster charging. Or snag the MagSafe Wallet so you can keep your credit card attached to your phone. There are plenty of third-party accessories (you'll find quite a few in our guide), and MagSafe doesn't just have to be charging accessories like power banks or wireless chargers. There is a wealth of useful tools, from wallets, tripods, and camera cages to notepads and ring lights that can attach to the back of the iPhone and add extra versatility.
If you plan to use a case, get one that has MagSafe embedded inside to ensure a strong magnetic connection with Apple's accessories (non-MagSafe cases can interrupt MagSafe and make the magnetic connection weaker). All of the cases in our case guides are MagSafe-tested. And yes, a case is a smart investment because iPhones are made of glass, and glass breaks, even if Apple uses ceramic to strengthen it. We cracked an iPhone 16 Plus after a 4-foot drop to the pavement—that model's ceramic glass was supposed to be twice as strong as previous iPhones, too! Ouch. See our favorite cases for the iPhone 17, iPhone 16, iPhone 15, and iPhone 14 ranges.
What's New in iOS 27?
While last year's iOS 26 debuted the divisive Liquid Glass, iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 focus squarely on quality-of-life improvements, with a redesigned and much improved Siri AI assistant, easier Shortcuts, and lots of little tweaks to enhance speed and stability.
Siri AI doesn't just look different—now resembling a glass orb—it can also understand your personal context, pulling info from your messages, emails, or even photos, and helping you draft messages or find the right wine to pair with your dinner. Siri can also now pop up in the camera app to help you choose your next book or split a bill with friends.
Apple says iOS 27 is faster than ever, with app launches up to 30 percent faster, newly captured photos in your Photo Library loading up to 70 percent faster, and AirDrop transfers completing up to 80 percent faster. For more details, read our guide on the top features in iOS 27 and how to download it.
Charging Adapters for Your iPhone
Apple hasn't offered a charging brick in the box since the iPhone 12, so if you don't have one, we've got you covered with a few recommendations. Most of these are 30-watt chargers that will fast-charge most iPhones. If you want the fastest speeds on the iPhone 18 models, you'll need a 40-watt charger, and we have some picks for you.
Anker 511 Nano 3 30-Watt Charger for $16: This is one of the tiniest chargers we've tested, and the prongs fold up for even more space savings. It comes in fun colors, and it's nice and cheap.

The prongs fold so they won't scratch anything in your bag, and the 35-watt output is enough to fast-charge most iPhones and iPads. It's a mouthful, but essentially, it can boost power output up to 60 watts when needed. That means it's a more versatile charger that you can use for your MacBook Air and your iPhone.
The Right USB-C Cable
The problem with USB-C is that its capabilities are so vast, but not every USB-C cable supports every single function. You need to make sure the cable you buy supports video output, speedy data transfer, and fast charging if that's what you want. The cable Apple includes in the box can carry up to 60 watts of power, and that's pretty much it. You can use this cable to recharge a MacBook but maybe not a MacBook Pro under heavy load.

Get a MagSafe Portable Battery
The beauty of MagSafe is that you can pop a battery on the back of your iPhone, and you don't have to worry about any wires. This is our top recommendation, and it supports the Qi2 standard, so it will work with any device with Qi2. Get a 3-in-1 Wireless Charger
If you have an iPhone, there's a chance you have another Apple gadget, like AirPods or an Apple Watch. If so, you really should get a 3-in-1 charger for your home. We have tons of options in our Best Apple 3-in-1 Chargers guide, but this Belkin MagSafe model is our favorite. It has an elegant design and charges the iPhone and Apple Watch at maximum speeds, and you can pop your earbuds on the base to top them up. It won't work with the iPhone 16e unless you get a MagSafe case, and even then, you won't be privy to the faster and more efficient charging speeds.
Carry a MagSafe Wallet
Hate bringing a wallet with you everywhere? Stick it to the back of your iPhone! This Nomad leather wallet is classy and can hold about four cards. What makes it unique is that it features Apple's Find My, meaning you can track its location in the Find My app if you lose it. That does mean the wallet needs to recharge every once in a while, but you can conveniently recharge it with any MagSafe charger, no proprietary cable needed. (It should last around five months on a single charge.) Read our Best MagSafe Wallets guide for more options.
The MagSafe world is wonderful and weird. We have plenty more recommendations in our Best MagSafe Accessories guide, ranging from MagSafe camera cages and tripods to notepads you can magnetically stick to the back of your iPhone.
Avoid These iPhones
The iPhone 14 and older iPhones are probably available somewhere, but you shouldn't take the bait. They don't have the processing power to keep up with the latest software, and even if they do, they will have a much shorter software shelf life or lack modern features like USB-C. The only older iPhones worth considering at the moment are the iPhone 15 or iPhone 16 series, even better if it's the Pro models, if you can find them at low prices. The iPhone 16e is also another option, though only if you can find it at a steep discount.
The iPhone XS, iPhone XS Max, and iPhone XR are cut off from receiving the iOS 27 update, so they're especially ones to avoid. Without software support, your device will slowly become less secure and could become a slow, buggy mess.
The iPhone's Charging Port Is USB-C, Not Lightning
The iPhone 15 range ditched the long-standing Lightning port for USB-C, and it's in every iPhone since. This is the same charging port on iPads, MacBooks, Android phones, Windows laptops, and many more personal tech gadgets. USB-C is often called the “universal port” because it can technically handle various responsibilities. For example, you can plug in external displays and extend the iPhone's screen or connect the same USB-C accessories you might be currently using on your laptop, like SD card readers. Sadly, it does mean your Lightning accessories won't work unless you get dongles.
You can read more about what the port does here, but there are two important things to note:
The iPhone 15, iPhone 15 Plus, iPhone 16, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16e, iPhone 17, iPhone 17e, and iPhone Air support the USB 2.0 standard just like the iPhones before, so you'll max out at 480 megabits per second of data transfer speeds.
The iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo support the USB 3.0 standard and are capable of up to 10 gigabits per second of data transfer speeds.
What’s the Deal With eSIMs?
All iPhone 14 and newer devices completely ditch the physical SIM tray in the US, meaning you can no longer just pop your physical SIM inside to turn on cellular connectivity. Instead, you'll have to rely on an eSIM. You can read more about them here. This tech has been available in iPhones since the iPhone XS and XR, but now you have to use it. Apple has also started switching more global models to eSIM only, like the iPhone Air.) When you're setting up your new iPhone, you'll automatically be asked to transfer your number from your previous iPhone, and the whole process should take a few minutes without any hassle. (eSIMs are more secure than physical SIMs.) Once you transfer your number, your physical SIM card won't work anymore.
There's a chance you may still run into some issues, especially if you're coming from an Android phone (or want to switch back to an Android phone). You'll have to check with your carrier to get your cellular connection working again. It shouldn't take long, but it's not as simple as popping in a physical card.
How to Replace Your iPhone's Battery
If you don't want to spend the money to get a new iPhone, consider a fresh battery. If the biggest issues with your aging iPhone revolve around how long it lasts in a day, replacing the battery might make it feel brand-new. (Apple's iPhone 16, 16 Plus, and 16e have an easier-to-replace battery.)
Replacements for older iPhones are $89, and $99 or $119 for newer models. If that doesn't do the trick, read our guide on ways to fix your iPhone's problems or our guide on selling your iPhone to get the most money for it.
What Is the Action Button and Camera Control Button?
The Action Button debuted on the iPhone 15 Pro models, and it's now standard on every iPhone in the lineup. It sits above the volume rocker on the left edge of the phone. It effectively replaces the old Mute Switch, but think of it as just a configurable button. You can have it still control the mute function of the phone, or customize it (Settings > Action Button) to trigger the flashlight, a Voice Memo, or even launch an app or Shortcut.
Camera Control is another newer addition that debuted on the iPhone 16 series. On the right edge of the phone below the power button, press it to launch the Camera app, and you can press it to capture a photo or start recording a video. A light tap and swipe can move through different camera lenses or modes, but I found this annoying. (You can configure it by heading to Settings > Camera > Camera Control.) Press and hold this button, and you'll trigger Apple's Visual Intelligence. It'll use the camera to identify subjects in front of you, very much like Google Lens, so you can ask questions via Google or ChatGPT about what you're looking at.

China has the world’s largest active military force, the biggest tank inventory and the highest number of naval assets, while the United States leads by a wide margin in total military aircraft, according to 2026 data from Global Firepower compiled by Visual Capitalist. The rankings show how the balance of military strength varies depending on the measure used. China leads in three of the four categories, while the US has a substantial advantage in aviation assets and naval tonnage. Meanwhile, India ranks among the top five countries across all four measures, underlining its position as a major military power. The data compares the world's 10 largest militaries by active military personnel, tanks, military aircraft and naval assets. The active personnel figures exclude reserve forces and paramilitary personnel. China ranks first with 2.035 million active military personnel, followed by India with 1.431 million and the United States with approximately 1.333 million. Russia and North Korea are tied at fourth place, each with 1.32 million active personnel. Ukraine ranks sixth with 900,000, followed by Pakistan with 660,000 and Iran with 610,000. Ethiopia and Türkiye round out the top 10. North Korea’s large active force reflects its longstanding emphasis on land-based military strength and the security situation on the Korean Peninsula. However, personnel numbers alone do not indicate the quality of training, equipment, readiness or battlefield effectiveness. China leads the tank ranking with 5,870 tanks, followed by Russia with 5,630 and North Korea with 4,895. The United States ranks fourth with 4,666, while India is fifth with 3,913, as per the analysis by Visual Capitalist. Egypt ranks sixth with 3,620 tanks, followed by Pakistan with 2,677 and Iran with 2,675. Türkiye and Vietnam complete the top 10. North Korea’s third-place ranking illustrates why equipment inventories must be interpreted carefully. The country continues to operate older tank designs alongside newer systems. The United States has 13,032 military aircraft, placing it first in the ranking and ahead of Russia, China, India and South Korea combined. Russia ranks second with 4,237 aircraft, while China is third with 3,529, as per Visual Capitalist. India ranks fourth with 2,183 aircraft, followed by South Korea with 1,540, Japan with 1,429 and Pakistan with 1,397. Türkiye, Egypt and France complete the top 10. The US advantage reflects the breadth of its aviation fleet, which includes combat aircraft as well as transport planes, helicopters, trainers and aircraft supporting long-range operations. The gap is narrower when the comparison is limited to fighters and interceptors. According to the figures cited by Visual Capitalist, the US has 1,791 such aircraft against China’s 1,443, a lead of approximately 24%. This distinction matters because total aircraft numbers measure the scale of a fleet, not just its combat power. Transport aircraft and aerial refuelling tankers, for instance, help militaries move personnel and equipment and sustain operations far from home bases. China leads the naval inventory ranking with 841 vessels, followed by Russia with 747 and the United States with 465. India ranks fourth with 343 naval assets, ahead of Indonesia with 338, the report says. North Korea ranks sixth with 332 assets, followed by Thailand, Italy, Sweden and Sri Lanka. China’s large naval inventory is supported by a shipbuilding industry that combines extensive commercial production with military construction. Research by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) cited in the report has highlighted how Chinese shipyards, infrastructure and industrial capabilities can support naval modernisation. The comparison changes when naval fleets are measured by total displacement rather than vessel count. Visual Capitalist, citing Global Firepower’s fleet-tonnage ranking, places the United States first, with roughly 2.6 times China’s total fleet displacement. India ranks second globally in active military personnel, fifth in tank inventory, fourth in military aircraft and fourth in naval assets, according to the 2026 data. The figures place India among the leading military powers across all four categories, but the rankings also reveal different strengths among the countries. China has larger inventories of personnel, tanks and naval assets, while the US leads in total aircraft and fleet tonnage. These comparisons, however, should not be treated as definitive measures of military effectiveness. Equipment counts do not establish how well equipped or combat-ready a force is, how effectively its different services operate together, or how quickly it can mobilise supplies and reinforcements.
